**Fix:** Give every call expression and pipeline stage a stable node identity: declare them mergeable blocks in the KLN block tree, so the structural editor and the GumTree reconcile keep their ids across appends, inserts and wraps. Define `OpSite` as (statement BlockId, call node id, feature instance path, loop keys) without the root path. Add oracle ING-O-SITE-1: appending, inserting and wrapping stages in golden-product pipelines leaves the EntityIds of untouched calls unchanged.

**Section:** ANV Blends (parameter and stage tables), State of the art (Blends); MEC Dress-up features; contract 7.1 (blends as a research program)
**Problem:** Phase 1 blending is constant radius with `KeepEdge` overflow and equal-radius three-edge corners on "analytic and NURBS supports"; blends whose supports are earlier blends wait for phase 4, yet the default overflow is `RollOver` (stage 2). Phase 1 users will fail on unequal radii at a corner, mixed-convexity corners (a boss-base fillet meeting a vertical-edge fillet), vertices of valence four or more, fillets that must roll onto a neighbor, filleting the top loop after the vertical edges, chamfer-fillet corners, chains across smooth edges and variable radius. OCCT, the open reference the draft benchmarks against, already offers linear and law-driven radii on tangent chains with corner fills.
**Evidence:** ANV stage 1 row; `overflow` default `RollOver`; stage 4 "Blends on blends (rolling over earlier blends)"; MEC `overflow: Overflow = Auto`; ANV target "above OCCT 8.0's at stage 1" versus MEC "target 97% success at phase 2"; OCCT `BRepFilletAPI_MakeFillet` reference (https://occt3d.com/dev/doc/refman/html/class_b_rep_fillet_a_p_i___make_fillet.html, opened): `Add(R1, R2, E)` sets "a linear radius evolution law", `Add(L, E)` takes a law, `Add(E)` "builds a contour of tangent edges", failed corners are reported per vertex.
**Fix:** Re-scope stage 1: supports include Anvil's procedural blend, offset and swept surfaces, so sequential fillets work; `RollOver` overflow; valence-3 corners with unequal radii and mixed convexity by setback patches; chamfer-fillet corners; termination at smooth edges; linearly varying radius. Leave valence ≥ 4, Field-driven radii and G2/G3 sections to later stages and amend the contract's ordering to match. Until `RollOver` ships, both tabs default to `KeepEdge`. Build the blend benchmark in phase 0 (recognize and remove fillets on ABC parts, re-fillet with the recorded radii) and state one target per phase in both tabs.

**Section:** Tangential and degenerate cases; Surface-surface intersection; Blends
**Problem:** Every rolling-ball blend is tangent to its supports along its contact curves, so later Booleans, offsets, shells, drafts and second fillets near blended regions meet tangential contact along curves on most real parts. The draft gives no algorithm beyond "Curve classified `Tangential`; Booleans treat both sides with the tolerance rule". The critical-point Krawczyk system is singular along such curves, and the band where |distance| < τ around a contact has width about 2√(2τ/Δκ), which the tolerance rule would turn into spurious coincidence regions.
**Evidence:** ANV tangential-cases table; "Tangential intersections are ill conditioned ... √(2ε/Δκ)"; blend history records only `Modified { aspects: Boundary }` for supports, with no tangency certificate on the contact edges.
**Fix:** Record construction certificates on edges, `Continuity { order: G1 or G2, certified_by: (operation, site) }`, for blend contact edges, offsets of smooth edges and sweep seams. SSI and imprint consult them: face pairs sharing a certified G1 edge are not re-intersected along it, and a new surface tangent to a blend goes to a contact-curve algorithm that traces the reduced system (the critical-point system with the rank-deficient direction removed and h = 0), certifies it with an interval test, and imprints one tangential edge with τ = max(ρ, certified contact deviation). Add oracle families: fillet on fillet, cylinder resting on a plane, sphere in a cylinder, blend face cut by a plane through its contact curve.

**Section:** ANV Performance targets, Fidelity levels; MEC Performance budget; UIX Coarse-first preview pipeline; ING Previews, drags and incomplete code; PLT Budgets
**Problem:** The 2 s exact rebuild of a 200-feature part after an early edit and the 100 ms coarse preview "with dependent features updated" are not supported by any mechanism in the drafts. After an early edit every downstream input changes, so MEC's read sets and tool-body caching save nothing and drag specialization's forward slice is the whole chain; 1.2 s for about 200 certified operations leaves about 6 ms each for certified SSI and marching, `check_body`, relabeling and Merkle hashing, while Anvil expects certified SSI at up to twice OCCT's time. Coarser preview tolerances do not reduce the number of B-rep operations, and Anvil defines no geometry fidelity between `Preview` and certified results.
**Evidence:** ANV "Anvil share ≤ 1.2 s of the 2 s budget, with Kiln backdating unchanged features"; MEC "Kiln re-runs only features whose inputs changed"; UIX coarse stage "dependent features updated | ≤ 100 ms (contract)"; ING drag specialization "computes the forward slice of that literal"; ANV SSI target "at most 2× OCCT time on transversal cases"; MEC "drawing update after an edit to a 200-feature part in under 1 s", shorter than the rebuild it depends on.
**Fix:** (1) Define Anvil `Interactive` fidelity: the same Portable code with floating-point topology decisions validated after the fact (`check_body` plus Krawczyk verification of traced points), cacheable, never consumed by SignOff checks or releases; SignOff recertifies in the background. (2) State the 2 s target for `Interactive` and add a SignOff target (for example 10 s). (3) Define preview scope: within 100 ms, the dragged feature and as many downstream features as fit, in program order; the rest show stale geometry with a visible boundary. (4) Publish the 200-feature benchmark's operation mix and per-operation budgets, and run a phase 0 spike measuring certified SSI and Boolean cost on ABC face pairs before freezing the targets. (5) Restate the drawing target as "under 1 s after the rebuild completes".

**Section:** contract 7.2 (two-stage caching of entity-naming Ops; ruling ING-10 and ANV-5); ANV D-ANV-14; Persistence and versioning
**Problem:** The ruling that the geometric stage is "keyed without OpSite and shared across designs" yields almost no sharing. The key includes input ObjectIds, and the Body hash covers the EntityId section, so after the first named operation of a chain every input differs between designs, and between two calls of the same std feature; only label-free leaf operations share. The ruling also relies on, but does not state, the condition that the geometric core never reads input labels (R2-02).
**Evidence:** contract 7.2; ANV encoding "Sections. Topology tables, geometry pools, `EntityId`s, ..." under one Merkle hash; ANV "each operation runs as a site-independent geometric core, cached without the site and labeled with provisional ids".
**Fix:** Give every Body two identities: `GeomId` (geometry, topology and tolerances in the label-invariant canonical order of R2-02) and the full `ObjectId`. Key the geometric stage by input `GeomId`s; the core returns history in terms of input canonical positions; the relabeling stage, keyed by input `ObjectId`s and the OpSite, maps positions to EntityIds. State in 7.2 that the geometric stage must be label-invariant and reuse oracle ANV-O-LABEL-1. With this, std features called from different designs share every geometric result.

**Section:** ANV Transform, pattern, mirror; MEC Patterns and mirror; ING Kiln-held values (`.moved(by:)`)
**Problem:** `anvil::transform` keeps EntityIds for rigid motions and reflections, and MEC's `mirror` and Ingot's `move` lower to it. Combining a Body with a moved or mirrored copy of itself, the commonest symmetry idiom (`half + mirror(half, plane.yz)`), or two Instances of one Part in an assembly-level feature, puts identical EntityIds into one Boolean, which fails with `EntityIdCollision` or makes every query on the seed resolve to both copies. Roles also flip meaning under reflection (`side(left)` lands on the right).
**Evidence:** ANV transform row "EntityIds kept: identity for rigid motions, `Modified { aspects: Geometry }` for scaling and reflection"; the separate-id guarantee exists only for `anvil::pattern` ("an original and its mirror copy never share EntityIds"); "Within one Body, a duplicate EntityId fails the operation with `Internal::EntityIdCollision`"; MEC patterns and mirror use "`anvil::transform`, `anvil::boolean` (n-ary)".
**Fix:** Separate placement from copying. A transform whose source value is used again in the program (Ingot knows this from data flow) or that is written as `copy` creates ids `EID(kind, site, role: copy, [source id])` with a new `Copied { from, into }` record that lineage follows only on request (`seed.face(top).copies()`); a motion that replaces the Body in the data flow keeps ids. Reflection records `Mirrored`, so role queries can say `side(left, mirrored: true)`. Assembly-level features prefix ids with the Instance path.

**Section:** ING Entities and call sites (Loop indices); Patterns, loops and identity; MEC Patterns and mirror (`skip: [Int]`, `at_points`, `fill`, `by_density`); ANV Rust API (`OpSite`)
**Problem:** `OpSite` uses the positional iteration index by default and keyed iteration is opt-in; patterns name copies and skip instances by index. Patterns driven by geometry (`at_points`, `fill`, `by_density`, `along`) and loops over query results (`for e in body.edges(convex)`) therefore rename every later copy, retarget skip lists and break anchors when one element is inserted or removed. That is positional indexing under another name, contrary to the contract's "No positional indexing".
**Evidence:** ING "Loop indices | The iteration index, or the key of a `keyed` collection"; "`for x in keyed(holes, by: |h| h.label)` uses the key in place of the index" (opt-in); ANV `OpSite { path, indices: Box<[u32]> }`; MEC `skip: [Int] = []`; `by_density` runs Lloyd iterations that move every seed.
**Fix:** Make keys the default. Iteration over `Entity<K>` lists or resolved queries keys by EntityId; transform generators return keyed lists (`linear` keys `(i, j)` from the seed, `circular` the angular index, `at_points` the point's anchor EntityId, `fill` lattice coordinates from a declared origin, `by_density` each seed's initial key before Lloyd steps); plain integer ranges keep integer keys. Replace `skip: [Int]` with `skip: [Key]` and `OpSite.indices: [u32]` with `[SiteKey]`. The language service warns on positional keys over lists whose length depends on geometry.

**Section:** Booleans for every representation pair (D-ANV-20); Performance targets; State of the art (Mesh Booleans)
**Problem:** The chosen method (a global arrangement with indirect predicates on f64, exact classification, rounding with repair) is one to three orders of magnitude slower in published measurements than EMBER, yet its target is "≤ 70 ms on 8 cores, 2× EMBER" for a million triangles. The repair loop has no termination argument. The reason given for rejecting quantized input, EMBER's 15 nm grid, does not apply to a grid at Anvil's own resolution ρ = 2⁻³⁰ of the diagonal.
**Evidence:** EMBER (https://www.graphics.rwth-aachen.de/media/papers/339/ember_exact_mesh_booleans_via_efficient_and_robust_local_arrangements.pdf, opened): 34 ms for 1.2 M triangles on 8 cores; beam case 4.5 ms against 1,556 ms for the floating-point arrangement of Cherchi et al. 2020 and 18,018 ms for Mesh Arrangements; output is a polygon soup with T-junctions. Cherchi et al. 2022 (https://ar5iv.arxiv.org/html/2205.14151, opened): 0.14 s per frame at 200 K triangles, 19.5 s for 21.6 M, and exact-to-float conversion "is still elusive". trueform (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15905, opened) claims "up to two orders of magnitude faster" than prior art with valid, watertight output.
**Fix:** Replace the method decision with a phase 0 bake-off on Thingi10K pairs among (a) plane-based local arrangements on integer coordinates of the Body's ρ grid (2³⁰ to 2³¹ cells per diagonal, wider fixed-width predicates) with topology recovery into the half-edge Mesh, (b) trueform's topological aggregation once its license is confirmed, and (c) the current indirect-predicate design; set the million-triangle target from the winner. Bound the repair loop (fixed number of passes, collapse only edges shorter than 2ε, then `PrecisionExhausted`). Lower whole CSG expression trees to one n-ary arrangement so rounding happens once per tree.

**Section:** ANV Representation lattice (D-ANV-2), Conversions (Implicit → BRep); MEC Lattices and Field-driven geometry; contract section 5 `Body`
**Problem:** By the lattice, a B-rep part joined with an implicit lattice becomes an `Implicit` Body, which has no faces, edges, attributes or B-rep EntityIds, and in phase 1 converts back only to facet faces. Golden product 2 therefore loses its exact mounting holes, `HoleSpec` attributes, GD&T targets and drawings, although semantic PMI requires exact geometry and post-print machining of interfaces needs exact faces. "Without approximation" holds for the point set, not for the information the Body carries.
**Evidence:** ANV "anything ⊕ Implicit is an Implicit"; conversion table "Implicit → BRep ... 1 (facet), 3 (fitted)"; Implicit "No explicit edges"; CAx-IF PMI recommended practice v4.1 (https://www.mbx-if.org/home/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/rec_pracs_pmi_v41.pdf, opened): "PMI Representation (semantic) data shall only be used when exchanging exact geometry".
**Fix:** Add a phase 1 leaf-preserving conversion: where the active leaf of the Implicit is a B-rep distance leaf, the output face is that leaf's exact face with its EntityId and attributes, trimmed by the certified intersection with the implicit part; only regions where other leaves are active become facet faces. Alternatively allow a cellular Body whose `Material` region carries an implicit fill inside an exact B-rep boundary. Amend the contract's lattice sentence to "the least representation that holds both operands without approximating geometry or dropping B-rep faces that remain on the boundary".

**Section:** MEC Solver method (D-MEC-4), Platform notes, Oracles (MEC-O-SK-4), Molded and cast part design (D-MEC-18)
**Problem:** `anvil::solve_constraints` and `anvil::thickness` produce geometry and geometric Fields, which the contract restricts to the `Portable` grade, but MEC specifies faer sparse QR (runtime CPU-feature dispatch and rayon parallelism on by default, no reproducibility statement), says "Fused multiply-add use is fixed per platform class", accepts 1e-12 relative agreement across classes, and computes thickness Fields on the GPU with CPU refinement only near thresholds. Sketch geometry, wall-thickness checks and everything downstream would then differ in bits by ISA or GPU.
**Evidence:** MEC "Blocks above 64 unknowns use sparse column-pivoted QR from faer"; "Fused multiply-add use is fixed per platform class"; MEC-O-SK-4 "agreement within 1e-12 relative across classes"; D-MEC-18 "computed on GPU with exact CPU refinement near threshold values"; faer documentation (https://docs.rs/faer/latest/faer/, opened): `std` adds "cpu feature detection at runtime", `rayon` is "enabled by default", and no determinism guarantee is stated; contract 7.3: `Portable` is "the only grade for geometry".
**Fix:** Solver linear algebra runs on the `kernels` IR with canonical 512-bit lanes and fixed reduction trees; faer is allowed only in a configuration with fixed SIMD width, no runtime dispatch and a fixed reduction order that the determinism suite verifies. Delete the FMA sentence (explicit `mul_add` only in `detmath` and error-free transformations). MEC-O-SK-4 requires bit identity across the canonical class. In D-MEC-18 the GPU only locates candidate thin regions; canonical Field values come from the CPU (`Certified` grade).

**Section:** ING Sketches and constraints; MEC Solver method (step 4) and Diagnosis
**Problem:** A solved sketch point is returned as `Approx<Point3>` "whose bound comes from the solver's converged residual", but a residual is not a forward error bound: the position error is about ‖J⁻¹‖·‖r‖, large for nearly tangent arcs, nearly parallel lines and near-singular mates. A `Guaranteed` bound derived this way lets `Truth` decide checks wrongly. The convergence rule "below one hundredth of the smallest Anvil entity tolerance" (about 10⁻¹² m for a 0.1 m sketch) also fails on ill-conditioned but valid sketches.
**Evidence:** ING "Reading `s.c.center` after the solve returns `Approx<Point3>`, whose bound comes from the solver's converged residual"; MEC step 4 "Convergence requires the scaled residual below one hundredth of the smallest Anvil entity tolerance involved"; Anvil already certifies roots with Krawczyk elsewhere.
**Fix:** After each well-determined block converges, run a Krawczyk (or Kantorovich) test on the scaled system; the radius of the proven box is the `Guaranteed` bound and certifies a unique solution on the chosen branch. If the test fails, the bound is `Estimated` (an estimate of ‖J⁻¹‖ times the residual) and the report says why. Replace the absolute convergence rule with "residual small enough that the certified box radius is below the smallest entity tolerance", else `IllConditioned { block, condition }` with fixes.

**Section:** ANV Persistence and versioning (D-ANV-9); Versions and the cache
**Problem:** Bodies are re-encoded in the current encoding version, so a minor version that adds a column with defaults changes the ObjectId of geometrically identical results. Two trusted builders on different releases then write different ObjectIds for one OpKey into the shared cache, downstream keys diverge, and a release that records the results it cites cannot be re-verified bit for bit after an upgrade.
**Evidence:** ANV "A minor version adds optional sections or columns with defaults"; "Writers write only the current version"; "A Body decoded from an older encoding is re-encoded in the current version, so its content hash is an ordinary hash and needs no extra key"; KLN D-KLN-10 note: "A release records the class of every result it cites".
**Fix:** Hash a canonical form that is invariant across minor versions: optional sections and columns equal to their defaults are omitted from the hashed bytes. A major encoding change is a behavior change: it enters item 1 of the OpKey and is pinned in `ingot.lock`, and a writer is kept for every pinned major. Add oracle ANV-O-ENC-2: hashes of the golden corpus are unchanged across minor encoding releases.

**Section:** MEC Tolerancing › Specification model, Two dialects, one model (D-MEC-20); ING GD&T controls as types; ANV Attributes
**Problem:** The GD&T record cannot express constructs both standards use daily, so dialect validation, AP242 export and MEC's own NIST oracle cannot be complete. Missing: pattern and combined-zone specifications (ASME composite frames and simultaneous requirements; ISO 5458 CZ, CZR and SIM), ISO 14405-1 size specification modifiers (two-point, least-squares, maximum inscribed, minimum circumscribed, rank-order sizes, envelope), ISO 2692 material requirements as a governing standard, ISO 1101 intersection-plane, orientation-plane, direction-feature and collection-plane indicators, unequally disposed and offset profile zones, ASME irregular features of size, all-over, translation modifier and statistical tolerancing. Separately, a toleranced face that a later operation splits silently becomes separate zones under the attribute default `Copy`.
**Evidence:** MEC `GeometricTolerance { characteristic, zone (width; shape: Diameter, Sphere, Planes, Boundary), modifiers, datums, target }`; ISO dialect list (1101, 5459, 14405-1, 8015, 22081) has no 5458 or 2692; ISO 5458:2018 scope (https://www.evs.ee/en/iso-5458-2018, opened): zones "grouped together with location or orientation constraints ... through the use of the CZ, CZR or SIM modifiers", with maximum and least material requirements left to ISO 2692; ISO 14405-1:2025 exists (https://www.evs.ee/en/evs-en-iso-14405-1-2025, opened); ANV attribute split default `Copy`; MEC-O-DR-3 requires 100% of NIST semantic items, and NIST calls its FTC cases fully toleranced, with features that "may not be commonly used" (https://www.nist.gov/ctl/smart-connected-systems-division/smart-connected-manufacturing-systems-group/mbe-pmi-0, opened).
**Fix:** Extend the record: `zone: Zone { width, shape, disposition: Symmetric | Unequal(Length) | Offset(Length) }`, `segments: [Segment]` for composite and multi-segment frames, `pattern: Option<PatternSpec { combination: CZ | CZR | SZ | SIM, constraints }>`, `indicators: [PlaneIndicator]`, `size: Option<SizeSpec { operator: TwoPoint | LeastSquares | MaxInscribed | MinCircumscribed | Rank(..), envelope: Bool }>`, and the ASME default simultaneous requirement with `separate: true`. Add ISO 5458 and ISO 2692 to the ISO dialect. Give GD&T and PMI attributes the split policy `Fail`, so a split target forces re-specification. Ship the extended record in phase 1, because AP242 PMI export is phase 1.

**Section:** Two dialects, one model (D-MEC-20); Completeness (D-MEC-21); Stack-up and variation analysis
**Problem:** The dialect difference that most changes analysis results, ASME Rule #1 (envelope by default) versus ISO 8015 independency, is marked [unverified] and never reaches stack-up or variation analysis, which treat size as a plain `Tol<T>`. Completeness counts only the six small-displacement unknowns, so a cylinder with a position control but no size control, or a primary datum without a form control, is reported complete.
**Evidence:** D-MEC-20 "ASME applies the envelope principle by default and ISO applies independency [unverified]"; D-MEC-21 "Each toleranced shape aspect gets six small-displacement unknowns ... Free unknowns are under-specified directions"; Sigmetrix GD&T Advisor (https://www.sigmetrix.com/software/gdt-advisor, opened) shows "what features have been completely controlled", which is the coverage behavior to match.
**Fix:** Remove the marker and make the default specification operator part of each dialect: ASME envelope at maximum material for regular features of size unless independency is stated; ISO two-point size without form limitation unless Ⓔ. 3D variation samples form inside the envelope under ASME and independently under ISO. Completeness adds three checks to the DOF analysis: every feature of size has a size control, every surface has a form control (direct, general specification or envelope), and every datum feature has a form control suited to its precedence. Cite the invariance classes of the GPS model (ISO 17450-1) instead of the [unverified] marker, and add GD&T Advisor to the State of the art table as the implementation to beat.

**Section:** ANV Direct edits and defeaturing (`move_faces`); MEC Direct edits (D-MEC-9); UIX Push-pull
**Problem:** MEC promises that `anvil::move_faces` "regrows or removes blends", but Anvil's contract only re-intersects neighbors. Moving a face next to fillets, which is nearly every face of a real part, then fails or leaves blends with the wrong radius and broken tangency. Imported blends must first be recognized, which is phase 2, while UIX push-pull plans `move_faces` in phase 1.
**Evidence:** MEC D-MEC-9 "`anvil::move_faces` then re-intersects neighbors and regrows or removes blends"; ANV `move_faces` "Faces and a motion ...; neighbors re-intersected", phase 2; UIX phase 1 includes push-pull, which on non-cap faces "plans `offset_faces` or `move_faces`".
**Fix:** Specify blend handling in ANV's `move_faces`, `offset_faces`, `replace_faces` and `draft`: blends adjacent to moved faces (Anvil-made blends carry supports, radius and section; imported ones come from `recognize_aspects`) are removed, the edit is applied, and the blends are rebuilt with the same parameters and EntityIds (`Modified`), or the operation fails with `BlendRegrowFailed { blend, reason }` and the fixes "remove blend" and "reduce radius". Align phases: phase 1 push-pull on non-cap faces offers only `offset_faces` with this handling; `move_faces` arrives with ANV phase 2.

**Section:** ANV Names for other representations (Imported B-rep); `anvil::match_bodies`; ECO Identity across round trips
**Problem:** The two tabs give imported entities incompatible identities: Anvil uses a quantized geometric signature, ECO uses the source's persistent ID or "assembly path plus entity ordinal". Ordinals are positional and change when a supplier re-exports, and quantized signatures flip at quantization boundaries. `match_bodies` pairs faces by Hausdorff distance and overlap, so exactly the faces a supplier moved fail to match, and the mapping it produces is not reviewable.
**Evidence:** ANV "the discriminator is a geometric signature (surface type, quantized defining parameters and box at the face tolerance)"; "pairs faces by certified Hausdorff distance and overlap in the shared coordinate frame"; ECO "Otherwise the role is the structural path (assembly path plus entity ordinal), which is weaker".
**Fix:** One rule, owned by ANV and cited by ECO: imported EntityId = EID(kind, import site, role `imported`, [], discriminator), with the discriminator taken in order from the source persistent ID (AP242 persistent IDs, IFC GlobalId, native ids exposed by licensed translators), else an unquantized canonical signature (surface type plus a hash of the exact defining parameters as written) plus an adjacency signature, never an ordinal. `match_bodies` aligns rigidly first (`anvil::align`), then matches the attributed face-adjacency graph (type, area, normals, neighbors), and writes the confirmed mapping as a source artifact (`import_map(old, new, pairs)`) that reviewers see and later rebuilds reuse.

**Section:** contract section 6 canonical example; ING The query language (Selection); ANV Query resolution; AGT D-AGT-8; ANV-O-NAME-2
**Problem:** Geometric selectors (`longest`, `largest`, `first(along:)`) choose by rank, so when a parameter moves one entity past another, a query can resolve to a different entity with no error or note, which the contract forbids ("Never silently picks another entity"); `body.face(largest)` on a box whose two dimensions cross is the simple case. The tests sample only ±10% around current values, so they miss rank changes inside declared ranges: the canonical bracket declares `width` from 20 mm to 400 mm, and its `edge(longest, last(along: +y))` stops resolving below 40 mm, where the two 40 mm edges tie.
**Evidence:** contract section 6 `width: Length in 20mm..=400mm` with `rect(width, 40mm)` and `.edge(longest, last(along: +y))`; ING "Selection | `longest`, ... | Extremal choice ... singular forms fail on a tie"; D-AGT-8 "16 seeded parameter perturbations within declared ranges (default ±10%)"; MEC D-MEC-1 "geometric predicates ... only as filters".
**Fix:** (1) Rewrite the contract example to select by provenance, for example `base.face(role: end_cap).edge(role: side(r.top))` with the rect's named edge. (2) Allow selectors only after a provenance anchor or role filter, as D-MEC-1 already says; a selector over an unanchored set raises lint `ING-L-FragileSelector`. (3) D-AGT-8 and ANV-O-NAME-2 sample the full declared range, endpoints included, plus ±10% around the current value, and report `Note::RankSwap { at }` when the winner's lineage changes within the range.

**Section:** ELX Board geometry (D-ELX-6), DRC, Pours, planes and vias; contract 7.1 (`anvil-planar`)
**Problem:** The contract calls `anvil-planar` "exact integer-coordinate 2D geometry with lines and arcs", but its operations are not closed over integers: offsets and Minkowski sums with a disc create tangent points and arc intersections at irrational coordinates, and ELX approximates arcs for Booleans. Results must be rounded to the nanometre grid, so a fill generated exactly at the clearance can sit up to about 0.7 nm too close, and the exact integer DRC then flags Crucible's own fills or needs a hidden tolerance.
**Evidence:** contract 7.1 "exact integer-coordinate 2D geometry with lines and arcs (`anvil::planar::boolean`, `offset`, `distance`, `medial_axis`, Minkowski with a disc)"; ELX "Arcs are stored as three integer points"; "it approximates them for the Boolean and reconstructs them in the result"; DRC "Clearance tests compute exact segment, arc and polygon distances in integer arithmetic". Rounding a point to an integer grid moves it by up to √2/2 grid units.
**Fix:** State `anvil-planar` semantics as "exact predicates on stored integer geometry; constructions snapped to the grid in a declared direction". Every construction that feeds a rule snaps conservatively: fill regions round inward (away from obstacles), keep-outs outward, so derived geometry passes the exact DRC by construction. Arc reconstruction keeps an arc only when it passes the exact check, otherwise its polygonal approximation. Oracle: every derived fill in the DRC corpus passes the exact reference checker with zero tolerance.

**Section:** MFG Stock models (D-MFG-6); Material removal and machine collision simulation
**Problem:** Gouge and leftover checks read the narrow-band grid stock, so their accuracy is the grid spacing, yet the gouge oracle requires every planted gouge to be found. For golden product 1 at a 5 µm spacing, a 100 × 100 × 30 mm part has about 1.3 × 10⁹ surface cells and about 8 × 10⁹ band cells (roughly 60 GB of f64), against a 1 GiB memory target; at a spacing the laptop can hold (20 µm or more), shallower gouges go undetected.
**Evidence:** D-MFG-6 "In-process stock is an `Implicit` Body backed by a sparse narrow-band distance grid at a declared resolution"; "Gouge and leftover | Signed distance from simulated stock to the exact design B-rep ... Seeded gouge corpus: every planted gouge detected"; PLT "Memory with golden product 1 open | Under 1 GiB in total". Arithmetic: surface area about 0.032 m² divided by (5 µm)², times a band of ±3 cells.
**Fix:** Detect gouges independently of the stock: for every cutting move, compute the certified minimum distance between the tool's exact swept envelope and the design B-rep (`anvil::distance` against `anvil::swept_volume` per move, or `tool_contact` along it), which is exact and needs no stock. Use the stock only for leftover, rest machining and display, with adaptive refinement near the design surface and a stated `ErrorBound` per setup. Add tri-dexel stock with exact dexel endpoints as a candidate in the phase 1 benchmark.

**Section:** ANV Operations catalog (Blends, Construction, Mesh processing operations); MEC Dress-up features
**Problem:** The catalog lacks operations that Parasolid, ACIS, OCCT or code-CAD tools provide, and that MEC already calls: blends between non-adjacent face sets with hold lines, three-face (full-round) blends, constant-width (chordal) blends, convex hull of Bodies, general 3D Minkowski sums (only ball offsets exist), parametric law curves and surfaces from `Expr<T>`, and changing an existing blend's radius on any B-rep.
**Evidence:** MEC declares `face_fillet(... hold_lines ...)`, `full_round(...)` and `BlendProfile::ChordLength`, while ANV's `anvil::blend` takes only `edges`; ANV mentions convex hulls only as users of linear predicates; the OpenSCAD cheat sheet (https://openscad.org/cheatsheet/, opened) lists `hull()`, `minkowski()`, `offset()` and `text()` among its core operations; OCCT's fillet API (opened, see R2-07) accepts law-driven radii.
**Fix:** Add to ANV's catalog, with contracts, roles, errors and phases: `anvil::blend` variants `FaceFace { a, b, hold_lines }`, `ThreeFace { a, middle, b }` and `ChordWidth(Length)`; `anvil::hull` (exact on meshes and facet faces in phase 1; B-rep operands by support-function sampling with a stated bound); `anvil::minkowski` for meshes and convex B-rep operands (phase 2); `anvil::curve(Law(expr))` and `anvil::surface(Law(expr))` evaluated from the kernel IR with interval bounds; `anvil::edit_blend` for radius changes on Anvil-made or recognized blends. MEC maps its features to these names.

**Section:** MEC Phasing; Sketching (Entities); Deform, wrap, emboss and engrave; ANV Phasing
**Problem:** The phase 1 wedge (code-CAD and 3D printing) omits operations every code-CAD user expects on the first day: text (phase 2), emboss and engrave (phase 3), exact helices for printed threads (ANV phase 2, while MEC lists helix in phase 1), convex hull and Minkowski (absent), and variable fillets (phase 2). The wedge's competitors already offer these, so it loses on core idioms whatever the kernel's robustness.
**Evidence:** MEC `text` "| 2", "Deform, wrap, emboss and engrave ... Phase 3", helix "| 1" against ANV "exact helix 2" and phase 2 "helices"; OpenSCAD cheat sheet (opened): `text`, `hull`, `minkowski`, `linear_extrude(height, center, convexity, twist, slices)`.
**Fix:** Move into phase 1: sketch `text` with bundled fonts feeding `make_regions`; emboss and engrave on planar and cylindrical faces (developable wrap only); exact `anvil::curve(Helix)` and helical sweeps for threads; `anvil::hull` on meshes and facet faces; extrusion with twist and scale Fields (already in `sweep`). Keep general wrap and deform in phase 3.

**Section:** MEC Dress-up features, Profile features, Lattices, Phasing, Interfaces (operation groups); ANV Blends, Draft, Construction, Phasing, State of the art
**Problem:** Beyond the names already ruled on, MEC and ANV disagree on operations and phases, so MEC ships features before the operations they call. Neutral-plane draft (MEC 1, ANV 2); helix (MEC 1, ANV 2); setback vertex blends (MEC 2, ANV 3); conic and G2 blends (MEC 3, ANV 2); face fillet and full round (MEC 2, no ANV operation); freeform surfaces (MEC `std::mech::surf` 3, ANV boundary, fill, blend and match surfaces 2); lattices (MEC: a Wasm component emits implicits; ANV: native `anvil::lattice`); blend overflow default (`Auto` against `RollOver`); blend targets (97% at phase 2 against "above OCCT" at stage 1).
**Evidence:** The rows cited above in MEC (Dress-up table, Profile features, Lattices "Generation runs in a Wasm component", Phasing) and ANV (stage table, Draft "Phase 2", Construction, Phasing, State of the art).
**Fix:** ANV publishes one operation-to-phase table and MEC copies it verbatim. Resolve each pair: draft and helix in phase 1 in both tabs, or out of MEC phase 1; setback blends phase 3 in both; conic and G2 blends phase 2 in both; face fillet and full round use the R2-25 operations in phase 2; `std::mech::surf` exposes ANV's phase 2 surfaces in phase 2; MEC's `lattice` calls `anvil::lattice`, and `mech-lattice` becomes a cell-family generator; one overflow default; one blend target per phase.

**Section:** ECO Round-trip and differential suites; Identity across round trips; ANV Cellular topology (no seam, no degenerate edges), D-ANV-7
**Problem:** Two oracle pass lines cannot pass by construction. Anvil forbids seam edges and degenerate pole edges and keeps procedural surfaces (blends, sweeps, intersection curves) that AP242 receivers get only as B-spline approximations, so a self round trip cannot give "B-rep surfaces and curves bit-identical; same topology counts". OCCT's B-rep stores seam edges on closed periodic faces and degenerated edges at poles, so a differential read cannot give "Topology counts equal". Receivers that expect seams also need them on export, while Anvil writes seams only "where the target schema requires them".
**Evidence:** ECO "Self round trip | ... B-rep surfaces and curves bit-identical; same topology counts"; "Differential read | ... Topology counts equal"; ANV "No seam edges", "No degenerate edges", "STEP export inserts seams where the target schema requires them"; D-ANV-7 procedural geometry.
**Fix:** Define a topology normal form for comparisons (seams and poles removed, periodic faces unsplit, seam and pole counts reported separately) and apply it to both sides. Self round trip: analytic and NURBS geometry bit-identical; procedural geometry equal to its recorded B-spline approximation within the stored bound; topology equal in normal form. Export always writes seam edges and pole vertices, configurable per receiver profile, and records them in the translation report so persistent IDs map back to Anvil entities.

**Section:** Strategy and fidelity (D-ECO-3)
**Problem:** The statement that `espr` "reached version 0.4.0 in September 2026" is wrong: 0.4.0 was published on 20 September 2024 and is still the latest release, so the Rust EXPRESS tooling is stale, not merely young. The plan also treats schema code generation as the translator, while most of a STEP translator is the hand-written mapping from the AIM to the model and the CAx-IF recommended practices, which EXPRESS does not encode; early-bound Rust types for AP242's long form will also bloat the Wasm component.
**Evidence:** crates.io API for `espr` (https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/espr, opened): newest version 0.4.0, released 2024-09-20, five versions in total; ECO "one EXPRESS code generator serves STEP AP203, AP214, AP242, AP209, AP238, AP239 and IFC".
**Fix:** Correct the date and add the maintenance risk to the open questions. Split D-ECO-3 into three layers with separate estimates and oracles: (1) generated Part 21 reader and writer and entity types, with late-bound, dictionary-driven access for the long tail of AP242 entities to bound code size; (2) generated checkers for EXPRESS WHERE and uniqueness rules; (3) hand-written semantic mapping modules per application protocol and per recommended practice (geometry and topology, assembly structure, PMI, validation properties, persistent IDs), each with its own conformance cases. Plan layer 3 as the phase 1 critical path.

**Section:** MEC Surfacing (Continuity, Class-A evaluation, D-MEC-14); State of the art (Surface continuity and Class-A); ANV Blends (stage 4)
**Problem:** The tab claims Class-A capability through a check library, but Class-A work is an interactive modeling loop: control-vertex edits with live zebra and curvature feedback, and G2/G3 matching and blending across patch boundaries. Here CV editing arrives in phase 3 and goes through source edits, Kiln rebuilds and re-tessellation; G3 blend sections arrive in phase 4; highlight lines in phase 3. The continuity defaults are absolute (0.001 mm), which contradicts the scale-relative tolerance model for hull fairing and MEMS.
**Evidence:** D-MEC-14 "Class-A quality is a check library over analysis Fields, not a mode"; `edit_cv` "| 3"; ANV stage 4 "G3 sections for class-A surfacing"; MEC defaults "0.001 mm position, 0.02 deg normal angle, 2% curvature".
**Fix:** Replace "Class-A" in capability statements with "surface-quality checks" until the modeling loop exists. Specify a CV-drag fast path: a patch-local surface edit evaluated outside the full rebuild, with GPU zebra on the preview tessellation within 16 ms, committed as one Ingot edit on release; ship G2/G3 `match_surface` and `blend_surface` in the same phase as `edit_cv`. Express continuity defaults relative to the Body's resolution or size, with absolute overrides per design.

**Section:** ANV Worked example 1; Query resolution (fixes); ING The query language (Role)
**Problem:** Fixes are promised as "typed source edits", but the worked example offers `rib.face(side_front)`, which is not a role extrude produces (`side(e)` per profile edge) and would not compile. Helper-emitted profiles (`rect`, `slot`, `polygon`) have no documented names for their edges, so readable role queries such as "the rib's front side" cannot be written without falling back to geometric selection.
**Evidence:** ANV fixes list `"part.face(base.face(top), bounded_by: rib.face(side_front))"`; ANV extrude roles `side(e)` "per profile edge"; ING roles "declared by the creating feature with `#[roles(start_cap, end_cap, side(Edge))]`"; MEC's sketch example uses `r.left` and `r.bottom` without a specification.
**Fix:** Specify named sub-entities for every sketch helper (`rect`: `left`, `right`, `bottom`, `top` in the sketch frame; `slot`: `start_arc`, `end_arc`, `side_a`, `side_b`; `polygon`: `edge(k)` keyed from a declared start vertex) and the role form `side(r.bottom)`. Rewrite the worked example's fixes in that syntax. Add oracle ANV-O-NAME-5: every `Fix` emitted on the golden products and the ResolveError corpus compiles, resolves and matches its ranked description.

**Section:** Query resolution (D-ANV-15); contract ruling ANV-4
**Problem:** Accepting merged anchors by default suits references that use only the surface (sketch planes, up-to faces, mate axes) but not references that use the face's extent: edges for fillets, area selectors, GD&T and PMI targets and drawing dimensions. For those a merge changes meaning, as worked example 2 shows, and a note is easy to miss.
**Evidence:** D-ANV-15 "a merged entity still contains the referenced geometry, so resolving it changes extent but not meaning"; worked example 2 "A fillet on `f.edges()` now runs around the combined face".
**Fix:** Make the default `on_merge` depend on the consumer's declared use: `Surface` uses accept with a note; `Extent` uses (edges of a face, area, GD&T and PMI targets, drawing items) fail with `ResolveError::Merged { anchor, with, fixes }`, offering `on_merge: Accept` or the merged entity explicitly. Operations declare the use per `Query` parameter.

**Section:** HistoryRecord
**Problem:** The record kinds cannot express many-to-many rearrangements that n-ary Booleans produce, for example two coplanar overlapping top faces cut by a slot tool in one call, where each output piece merges parts of both inputs. The intermediate pieces are neither inputs nor outputs, so the coverage property gives them no place.
**Evidence:** "Every input entity is unchanged in the output, or is the subject of exactly one same-kind record"; `Split { from, into }` and `Merged { from, into }`; D-ANV-19 n-ary expressions.
**Fix:** Allow transient entities in records, with ids computed as usual and a `Transient` flag, or add `Rearranged { from: [EntityId], into: [EntityId], overlap: [(usize, usize)] }`; extend the coverage property and ANV-O-NAME-1 to match.

**Section:** Transform, pattern, mirror (pattern reuse)
**Problem:** Reusing the first copy's intersections requires target faces "congruent ... checked exactly on the defining parameters", but rotated defining parameters are rounded, so exact equality almost never holds for circular patterns. The "5,000 cooling holes" claim then holds only for translational patterns on planes.
**Evidence:** "each copy meets congruent target faces (checked exactly on the defining parameters)"; "Five thousand cooling holes in a plate then cost one hole's intersection work".
**Fix:** Decide congruence with the tolerance rule (certified distance between the transformed and the actual target below τ), add one rotation rounding to reused results' bounds, and state the claim separately for translational, circular and mirror patterns, with an oracle on a circular pattern of holes in a cylinder.

**Section:** Implicit meshing (step 2, certify cells)
**Problem:** Certification demands that one axis-aligned partial derivative exclude zero, which fails at every sharp corner of a CSG implicit (at a box corner the gradient is one of ±x, ±y, ±z), so those cells stay `Uncertified` and their Hausdorff bound is only `Estimated` on the commonest inputs.
**Evidence:** "Refinement continues until each surface cell is monotone: the interval enclosure of one partial derivative excludes zero"; "Cells that reach λ without this property are flagged `Uncertified`".
**Fix:** Certify monotonicity along any direction d: accept a cell when the interval enclosure of ∇f·d excludes zero for a d chosen from the cell's gradient cone (for example the normalized sum of the active leaves' gradients), which certifies box corners and CSG edges; keep the axis directions as a fast first test.

**Section:** ANV Blends (implicit fallback); MEC Errors and approximations (D-MEC-2)
**Problem:** The fallback patch joins the exact blends with "a G0 seam whose gap is measured". A gap above the edge tolerance makes the Body invalid, and one below it still leaves a visible crease in a fillet; the polynomial smooth union also departs from a circular section by an amount that is not stated in advance.
**Evidence:** "The patch joins the exact blends with a G0 seam whose gap is measured"; "a smooth implicit union of the support faces' exact distances, with blend radius matched to r".
**Fix:** Fit the fallback patch with G1 boundary constraints to the neighboring exact faces (constrained least squares, as `match_surface` does); make the seam a tolerant edge with τ equal to the certified gap, failing with `ToleranceGrowth` beyond τ_cap; state the maximum deviation of the smooth union from the rolling-ball section as a function of r.

**Section:** Oracles (ANV-O-XF-1)
**Problem:** "Round trip within one ulp per coordinate" cannot hold for general rotations: applying a rounded rotation matrix and its inverse in binary64 accumulates several rounding errors per component, so the oracle fails on correct code.
**Evidence:** ANV-O-XF-1 "(round trip within one ulp per coordinate)".
**Fix:** State the bound as a multiple of the largest coordinate's ulp derived from the 3×3 product error bound (for example 8 ulp per round trip), and keep exact equality for translations on the frame grid and axis permutations.

**Section:** Mates (CoordSys from `csys(query)`); Interference and clearance (dynamic interference); Kinematics and motion
**Problem:** Two guarantees are overstated. A `CoordSys` derived from a face centroid or an edge midpoint moves when the face changes shape, with no `ResolveError`, contrary to "never a silent move". The dynamic-interference sampling rule guarantees that no contact between samples is missed, but a clearance violation between samples can be missed, while motion studies `require(min_clearance(...) > 0.5mm)`.
**Evidence:** MEC "`csys(query)` derives one from geometry: ... a planar face's centroid" and "a failed resolution is a `ResolveError` on the mate, never a silent move"; "Under that bound, no contact between samples is missed"; `study.require(min_clearance(study, housing, wheel) > 0.5mm)`.
**Fix:** Classify `csys` derivations as stable (axes, circle centers, vertices) or shape-dependent (centroids, midpoints, box centers) and attach `Note::ShapeDerivedFrame`, which release checks may forbid. Report sampled clearance as the interval [sampled minimum − maximum relative displacement, sampled minimum] and decide `min_clearance` checks three-valued, or use conservative advancement as MFG does.

**Section:** Drawings (Dimensions; associativity)
**Problem:** Many drawing dimensions attach to view-dependent curves that are not B-rep entities: silhouettes of cylinders and tori, projected tangent edges and section-cut boundaries. The tab attaches every dimension by `Query` on model entities and does not say how these references are named or re-resolved.
**Evidence:** "Dimensions | ... attached by `Query`"; "every drawing item references model entities by `Query`"; `anvil::silhouette` exists only as an analysis.
**Fix:** Add view-scoped references: `view.silhouette(face_query, side: Min | Max, along: dir)` and `view.section_edge(cut, face_query)`, resolved through the view's projection and the face's EntityId and failing with `ResolveError` when the silhouette disappears; include dimensions to silhouettes in MEC-O-DR-2.

**Section:** MEC Model-based definition (Non-B-rep bodies)
**Problem:** Semantic PMI eligibility is decided per Body representation, but by the lattice a B-rep Body can contain facet faces after a mixed Boolean with a mesh, and the CAx-IF practice restricts semantic PMI to exact geometry. A control whose target includes a facet face would be exported as semantic PMI on tessellated geometry.
**Evidence:** MEC "Mesh, implicit and SubD bodies export presentation-only PMI, flagged"; ANV "Mesh ⊕ BRep ... are B-reps whose faces keep their native geometry"; CAx-IF PMI v4.1 (opened) "PMI Representation (semantic) data shall only be used when exchanging exact geometry".
**Fix:** Decide per target face: controls whose targets include facet faces export as presentation only, with a translation-report entry, and `check::standards` flags semantic controls on facet faces at design time.

**Section:** ING Kiln-held values (`convert`); Approximate values as inputs; ANV Conversions (D-ANV-21)
**Problem:** Ingot wraps converted Bodies in `Approx<Body>` and adds measurement bounds of driving inputs to "the result Body's accumulated ErrorBound", while Anvil keeps per-face conversion bounds in the Body and defines `body.error()` as their maximum. Geometric error then lives in two places with different meanings (representation error against input uncertainty), and `Approx<Body>` makes `Estimated` fits fail as inputs (ING6403) although the Body already records its bound.
**Evidence:** ING "`body.convert(into: Mesh, tolerance: 0.01mm)` returns `Approx<Body>`"; "the bound is recorded in the call's accumulator and added to the result Body's accumulated `ErrorBound`"; ANV D-ANV-21 and `Body::error()`.
**Fix:** `convert` returns `Body`; representation error lives only in Anvil's per-face bounds. Bounds of `Approx` arguments go to an `InputSensitivity` record on the feature call, which variation analysis reads, not into `body.error()`.

**Section:** The query language (Geometric filters)
**Problem:** Writing a filter range as a tolerance (`radius: 3mm ± 0.05mm`) creates a tolerance site, and D-ING-4 records every tolerance a feature receives for PMI and variation analysis, so a selection range can surface as a manufacturing tolerance.
**Evidence:** ING "`radius: 3mm ± 0.01mm` ... a range or `Tol` argument means membership"; D-ING-4 "Every feature call records the tolerances it receives, so variation analysis, dialogs, PMI and `tolerances(x)` can find them".
**Fix:** Filters accept ranges (`radius: 2.95mm..=3.05mm`) or `near(3mm, within: 0.05mm)`; passing a `Tol` to a filter is a compile error whose fix rewrites it as a range.

**Section:** Intervals without rounding modes; Platform notes (FMA row)
**Problem:** TwoProduct uses `mul_add` "where the CPU has FMA", but Wasm, including every browser build, has no deterministic fused multiply-add instruction, so `f64::mul_add` falls back to a software emulation there and every interval product in the browser becomes much slower than the Dekker path. The stabilization of `next_up` is also left [unverified].
**Evidence:** ANV "TwoProduct uses `mul_add` where the CPU has FMA and Dekker splitting elsewhere"; Rust documentation (https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.f64.html, opened): `mul_add` "is guaranteed to be the rounded infinite-precision result", which a target without an FMA instruction must emulate; ANV Platform notes: relaxed SIMD is nondeterministic and never emitted.
**Fix:** State that wasm32 builds always use Dekker splitting for TwoProduct and for the division and square-root remainders, and native builds choose FMA by ISA level; both give the same exact error term. Verify the stabilization release of `next_up` and `next_down` and remove the marker.

**Section:** UIX From gesture to Ingot edit (ranking rule 1); ING Derivatives
**Problem:** Edit-plan ranking uses derivatives of the dragged quantity with respect to literals, but derivatives through Anvil operations need `anvil::shape_velocity`, which is phase 2, while direct manipulation is phase 1, and ING then falls back to dependence only. UIX does not say what the phase 1 ranking is.
**Evidence:** UIX "The nearest single literal with a non-zero derivative ranks first"; ANV `shape_velocity` "Phase 2"; ING "An Op without a tangent rule makes the derivative fail ... and the UIX ranking falls back to dependence only".
**Fix:** State the phase 1 ranking: provenance first (the literal of the call whose OpSite and role created the dragged entity, for example the extrude distance for an end cap), then IIR dependence distance; derivatives refine the ranking from phase 2.

**Section:** MFG Core manufacturing types (`Toolpath` as a wire Body)
**Problem:** A finishing toolpath has millions of moves; storing each move as a B-rep edge with a 128-bit EntityId, a lineage set, history records and a `kinds` map entry multiplies memory and hashing cost by orders of magnitude over a compact polyline.
**Evidence:** MFG `path: Body // wire Body`, `kinds: Map<EntityId, MotionKind> // per path edge`; ANV stores EntityIds, tolerances, lineage sets and history records per entity.
**Fix:** Store a toolpath as a wire Body with one edge per contiguous run of one motion kind, each carrying a `Polyline` or arc-spline curve with per-vertex Field samples; address single moves by (edge EntityId, vertex index), which is not a persistent name. State a size target (for example 10⁷ moves under 400 MB).

**Section:** Subdivision surfaces (Limit evaluation); Representation lattice
**Problem:** SubD ⊂ BRep is declared a lossless inclusion, but near extraordinary vertices with semi-sharp creases the limit is evaluated by subdivision to a finite depth, because Stam's method does not apply there, so those faces are exact only up to an unrecorded depth-dependent error.
**Evidence:** "Feature-adaptive subdivision to a fixed depth, then patches"; "Stam's evaluation ... does not address creases ... Anvil uses it inside the adaptive scheme only for crease-free neighborhoods".
**Fix:** Give subdivision-limit faces a certified evaluation bound near crease and extraordinary-vertex configurations (the geometric convergence of subdivision gives a computable bound per depth), record it as a conversion bound, and state the inclusion as exact except in those neighborhoods, where the recorded bound applies.

**Section:** Geometry types (D-ANV-7); Intersections › Building blocks
**Problem:** Procedural geometry can nest without limit (an offset of a blend between an offset and a sweep), and every evaluation, enclosure and cache certification of a nested surface solves the inner definitions again, so cost and enclosure width grow with depth; the draft states no limit or fallback.
**Evidence:** D-ANV-7 "Offset, intersection, sweep, blend and subdivision-limit geometry stays procedural, with exact evaluation plus a cached, certified NURBS approximation"; bounds use "its cached Bézier approximation plus the certified approximation error".
**Fix:** Add a nesting budget per face (for example depth 3): a construction whose inputs exceed it uses its inputs' certified NURBS caches as exact inputs, records their bounds as conversion bounds under the propagation rules of R2-03, and reports `Note::ProceduralFlattened`. State how caches of nested definitions are certified (Taylor models or interval Newton on the defining system) and measure the cost on blend-heavy ABC parts.

**Section:** MEC Part features; ING Kiln-held values (prelude frames)
**Problem:** The part-feature catalog has no reference geometry beyond the world planes and named `csys` values: no offset plane, plane at an angle, mid-plane between faces, plane through three points, tangent plane, axis of a face or through two points, or construction point on a curve. SOLIDWORKS, NX, Creo and CATIA users rely on these to place sketches, mirrors and patterns.
**Evidence:** MEC part-feature sections (profile, holes, dress-up, patterns, split, direct edits, deform, derived parts, configurations, lattices, machine elements) list none; ING prelude defines "the planes `plane.xy`, `plane.yz` and `plane.xz`"; MEC's drawing example uses `p.csys("mid").plane(yz)`.
**Fix:** Add `std::mech::refgeom` in phase 1: `plane.offset(from, d)`, `plane.at_angle(about: axis, angle)`, `plane.mid(a, b)`, `plane.through(p1, p2, p3)`, `plane.tangent(face, at)`, `axis.of(face)`, `axis.through(p1, p2)` and `point.on(curve, at:)`. Each returns a `CoordSys`-anchored value re-resolved through its queries, with handles for direct manipulation and typed `ResolveError`s.

**Section:** CONTRACT 7.2 (two-stage caching); ANV "EntityId", "Persistence and versioning"; KLN "Keys and behavior versions", "Revisions and lifecycle states" (D-KLN-26); FLX "Fields and errors (`flux-field`)"
**Problem:** Every identity that caching, early cutoff, revisions and approvals use hashes entity names, and names hash upstream `OpSite`s transitively through "generating entity ids". The "site-free geometric stage" is keyed by its inputs' `ObjectId`s, which contain those names. So it can be shared across designs only for an operation whose inputs carry no names, and a refactor that changes no geometry (the language service's "extract feature" or "inline binding", which change feature instance paths) changes every downstream Body and Field `ObjectId`. Contract 7.2's cross-design sharing, D-KLN-26's promise and early cutoff after refactors therefore cannot hold as specified.
**Evidence:** ANV: the Body encoding's sections hold "`EntityId`s, tolerances, attributes, lineage summary"; rows are ordered by Morton code "then `EntityId`", and "a row ends a leaf when a hash of its EntityId has its low 8 bits zero". EntityId `inputs` are "The EntityIds of the generating entities". KLN keys every Op by "Ordered `ObjectId`s of every input value". FLX: `pub domain: DomainRef, // Body content hash plus EntityIds`. D-KLN-26: an edit that leaves the definition unchanged ("a refactor, a comment, a change elsewhere in the repository") "never invalidates a release".
**Fix:** Give every Body two identities in `base`. `GeometryId` hashes the canonical encoding with names, lineage and name-keyed attributes removed, rows ordered by spatial key only and entities numbered in that order; `ObjectId` hashes the full named encoding. Amend 7.2: "The geometric stage of an entity-naming Op is keyed by its inputs' `GeometryId`s. It numbers new entities canonically and refers to input entities by canonical number. The relabeling stage is keyed by the geometric output's id, the `OpSite` and the inputs' name maps, and it assigns `EntityId`s." Flux results key on `GeometryId` plus the canonical numbers of the entities their conditions reference. D-KLN-26's `ItemDefinition` and approval digests use `GeometryId` plus PMI attached by canonical entity number. New ANV oracle: two designs that build the same geometry at different sites share every geometric-stage entry along a 20-operation chain.

**Section:** CONTRACT 5 (`Labels`); KLN "Memoization, verification and backdating", "Distributed and remote evaluation", "CRDT over the syntax tree", "Export control", Rust API (`Label`, `DataClass`)
**Problem:** Kiln is said to "join" labels, but three mechanisms lose or leak them. Backdating keeps `changed_at` when bytes are unchanged, so an input relabelled from confidential to ITAR with identical bytes never reaches its dependents. `DataClass` is one string, so the join of two incomparable classes (two export regimes, two customer scopes) cannot be represented. And a live document is one Loro replica per package, so a participant who "does not satisfy a label" still receives every CRDT operation of the labelled blocks.
**Evidence:** Contract 5: "`DataClass` (public, internal, confidential, export-controlled with regime and classification) ... Joined through every derivation by Kiln". KLN: "If the new value equals the old one, keep `changed_at` (backdating)"; `pub struct DataClass(SmolStr)`; "Organizations add classes such as `cui` or `customer:<name>`"; D-KLN-22 "one document per package"; "a participant who does not satisfy a label sees neither the labelled content nor its geometry". A replica must hold every causally prior operation to converge, so a relay cannot filter operations per recipient inside one document.
**Fix:** (1) Contract 5: `Labels` is a product lattice: `level` (public < internal < confidential), `controls: Set<(Regime, Classification)>`, `scopes: Set<Scope>`, `integrity`, `licences: Set<DataLicence>`. The join takes the maximum level and the union of each set, and a principal may read only if it satisfies every element. (2) KLN: a node's label is a separate memo output with its own `changed_at`. Verification re-joins labels from current inputs even when the value backdates, and a shared-cache hit returns only the value, with the label recomputed locally. (3) An encryption domain is keyed by tenant and canonical label set. (4) The unit of live replication is (package, label set). Blocks labelled above a document's label live in a separate document that only cleared participants receive, and the relay refuses moves into a lower-labelled document. (5) Extend `repo/labels`: relabelling an input with unchanged bytes updates every dependent label with zero re-execution, and an uncleared participant receives zero operations of a labelled document.

**Section:** ING "Strict, ordered, and failure-aware" (D-ING-11), "Resource limits"; KLN "Errors as values" (D-KLN-6)
**Problem:** `try` and wildcard `err(e)` arms catch any `Failure`, and nothing excludes environmental failures (out of memory, device loss, cancellation, a budget exhausted mid-run). Nor does anything exclude a `DependencyFailed` whose upstream was environmental. A feature can therefore take its fallback branch because a worker ran out of memory, and Kiln caches the fallback geometry as a deterministic value. This breaks principle 4 and can poison the shared cache.
**Evidence:** ING: "`Failure` is an extensible union ... a match over `Failure` needs a wildcard arm"; "`try e` turns propagation into a value of type `Result<T, Failure>`"; "When the host cannot supply memory ... evaluation fails with an environmental `ResourceExhausted`, which Kiln never caches". KLN: "A node that needs a failed value fails with `DependencyFailed { upstream }`"; "Exhausting a budget mid-run is an environmental failure and is never cached".
**Fix:** Contract 7.2 and ING define two disjoint classes. A deterministic `Failure` is catchable and cached. An environmental `Abort` covers cancellation, `ResourceExhausted`, device loss, budget exhaustion, worker loss, an unavailable retired version and the limits of R3-04. `Abort` is not a `Failure`: `try` cannot observe it, it propagates to every transitive dependent, and no node that observed one writes a memo entry, CAS object or attestation. `DependencyFailed` wraps only deterministic failures. New oracle `kiln/abort`: inject environmental faults at random Ops in 10,000 runs; every value that reaches the memo or shared cache equals the fault-free run's value.

**Section:** ING "Resource limits", "Strict, ordered, and failure-aware"; KLN "Scheduling and parallelism"
**Problem:** Ingot's claim that every evaluation ends in a value or a typed failure is false. Every limit applies per feature call, and each feature call is a separate Kiln node with fresh limits. A feature that calls itself with a new argument (`f(n) = f(n + 1)`) therefore builds an unbounded chain of nodes, and Kiln detects only a node that reappears on its own stack. Total work is also unbounded: 10⁹ steps per call times any fan-out times depth.
**Evidence:** ING: "Limits apply per feature call ... Feature calls and `#[memo]` function calls are Kiln nodes with their own limits ... Termination still holds, because every call is bounded and call depth is bounded"; the 2,048-frame depth limit is a "Default per feature call". KLN: "When a node demands a node already on its own active stack, Kiln returns `EvalError::Cycle`".
**Fix:** Kiln enforces two evaluation-wide limits as environmental `Abort`s (R3-03), so they never change a cached value. One is a demand-depth limit on nested node demands (default 10,000); the other is an aggregate fuel governor per Evaluation, taken from the request's budget. Restate ING's guarantee: "every node terminates with a value or a typed failure; every Evaluation terminates or aborts". New oracle ING-O-24: `f(n) = f(n + 1)` aborts with `DemandDepthExhausted` on every Tier 1 target and leaves no memo entry.

**Section:** KLN "Graph model" (Feature key); CONTRACT 7.2; ING "The incremental contract with Kiln"
**Problem:** KLN keys a feature node without its `OpSite`, yet the feature's result carries `EntityId`s that hash the feature instance path. Two `bracket()` calls with equal arguments at different sites then share one cached result with identical `EntityId`s. `left + (right |> move(x: 100mm))` then fails with `Internal::EntityIdCollision`, and `created_by: right` selects nothing. Contract 7.2 covers only entity-naming Ops and says nothing about feature nodes.
**Evidence:** KLN graph model: "Feature | feature identity, package closure hash, argument `ObjectId`s". ING: "A feature call is a node keyed by the feature's code hash, its `OpSite`, ... the `OpSite` is needed because entity names depend on it". ANV: `site` is "the feature instance path plus a call-site key"; "Within one Body, a duplicate EntityId fails the operation with `Internal::EntityIdCollision`".
**Fix:** Add to contract 7.2: "Every node whose value carries `EntityId`s (feature calls, entity-naming Ops, query resolutions) includes its `OpSite` in its key; cross-site sharing happens only in the site-free geometric stage of Ops (R3-01)." KLN's Feature key gains `OpSite`. New oracle `kiln/sites`: two equal-argument calls at different sites yield distinct `EntityId`s, and their union succeeds.

**Section:** ING "Entities and call sites"; KLN "CRDT over the syntax tree", "Storage format"; ECO "Package registry"; CONTRACT 5 (`EntityId`)
**Problem:** `OpSite`, and so every entity name, depends on Loro node ids that cannot be derived from source text. The same text can get different names after a Git round trip, after re-typing a statement, and in a registry package. ECO publishes packages without block maps, so ING's ordinal fallback applies to them. Inserting one statement into a std feature then renames entities in every dependent design on upgrade.
**Evidence:** ING: statement identity is "The `BlockId` of the enclosing statement block in the live document"; "A file outside any repository ... gets `BlockId`s derived from item paths and statement ordinals"; an outside edit "matches blocks by GumTree, so most `BlockId`s survive". KLN: "Block identities are Loro tree node ids"; "`crucible export git` writes Ingot text and lockfiles". ECO never mentions `BlockId`s or block maps.
**Fix:** Define statement identity from text in ING and contract 5. A `let` statement's identity is (item path, arm path, binding name), which ING1102 already makes unique per block. An unnamed statement's identity is (item path, arm path, nearest preceding binding name, ordinal after it). Renaming a binding is a refactor that writes `#[was(old_name)]`, which preserves the identity until the next edition. Loro node ids map onto these identities for collaboration only and never enter `OpSite`. New oracle (ING-O-10 and ANV): export to Git, re-import and rebuild; every `EntityId` is unchanged.

**Section:** ING "`Approx<T>` and `Truth`", "`require` and checks", worked example 3; FLX "Fidelity modes", "The error budget"; KLN "Progressive results"; AGT "Method catalog"; CONTRACT 5 (`CheckOutcome`)
**Problem:** Four tabs give four rules for deciding a check. ING decides on disjoint enclosures and makes any `Indicator` bound `Undecided`. FLX reports interactive bounds as `Indicator` and adds a consumer-side margin of three times the estimate; KLN adds a `Provisional` status. AGT's `CheckOutcome` has no `Undecided`, while ING adds `Error` and `Skipped`, so read literally every interactive Flux check is `Undecided(UnknownError)`.
**Evidence:** ING: "`Undecided(UnknownError)` | Any bound is `Indicator` or `Unknown`"; example 3 calls 112 ± 20 MPa against a 165.6 MPa limit `Undecided` because "FLX's interactive margin rule needs a margin of three times the estimate", though the enclosures are disjoint. FLX: discretization estimator "`Indicator` (residual)"; "`Pass` or `Fail` only with a margin of at least 3× the estimate". KLN: "Checks evaluated on `Preview` or `Interactive` results are reported as `Provisional`". AGT: `pub status: CheckStatus, // Pass | Fail | Error | Skipped`. Section 14 lists no `Undecided` edit for AGT.
**Fix:** One decision rule, owned by ING and applied to `if`, `require` and query `where:` alike: disjoint enclosures decide, subject to the check's `evidence`. Producers own their bounds. FLX reports interactive bounds already multiplied by the calibrated factor, labels them `Estimated { calibration }`, and drops the 3× rule. Contract 5 defines one `CheckOutcome { verdict: Pass | Fail | Undecided { reason, needed } | Error(Failure) | Skipped { reason }, fidelity, evidence, value, limit, margin, severity, source }`. "Provisional" becomes the derived predicate "fidelity below the declared one", not a variant. Add AGT to section 14's `Undecided` edit.

**Section:** CONTRACT 5 (`ErrorBound`, `ErrorBudget`, `Approx<T>`); FLX "Fields and errors"; COV "Error budget"; ING "`Approx<T>` and `Truth`"
**Problem:** `ErrorBudget` has three incompatible shapes, and the ruling that `Approx<T>` carries one cannot be implemented as written. FLX's struct cannot express "not quantified" and has no model-form component. COV's struct has four components and is generic, and the contract lists seven. `ErrorBound.value` is a bare `f64`, and `total(norm)` combines components measured in different norms, which means nothing for a scalar.
**Evidence:** FLX: `pub discretization: ErrorBound, pub algebraic: ErrorBound, ...`; `pub fn total(&self, norm: Norm) -> ErrorBound`. COV: `pub struct ErrorBudget<D> { discretization, solver, input, model_form }`. Contract 5: "named components (discretization, solver, geometry conversion, input and tolerance, model form, surrogate, interpolation) ... A not-quantified component is never treated as zero". ING: `bound: ErrorBound`; "reducing a Field yields an `Approx` whose bound is the budget's total". Ruling ING-2 "carries an `ErrorBudget`" has no matching ING edit in section 14.
**Fix:** One definition in `base`. `ErrorBound<Q> { value: Q, norm, kind }`; `enum Component<Q> { Quantified(ErrorBound<Q>), NotQuantified { reason } }`; `ErrorBudget<Q> { parts: BTreeMap<ErrorSource, Component<Q>>, total: Component<Q> }`. `ErrorSource` is the contract's list plus temporal, quadrature, floating point and statistical. The total is `NotQuantified` if any part is, and its kind is the weakest part's. `Approx<T>` carries `ErrorBudget<T::Delta>` restricted to `Pointwise` and `Goal` norms. A Field reduction is `Quantified` only when Flux estimated that functional, otherwise `NotQuantified`, so comparisons on it are `Undecided`. Add the ING edit to section 14.

**Section:** CONTRACT 6 (canonical example); FLX "Honest reporting of singular quantities", "Solve plans"; ING worked example 3; AGT "Text descriptions"; UIX "Running and exploring results"
**Problem:** The canonical check takes a peak stress next to a clamped face, and linear elasticity makes stress singular where a clamped face meets a free face. By Flux's own rule such a check can only report `Undecided`, yet AGT and UIX show it passing with margins. ING example 3 claims a `Guaranteed` ± 1.5 MPa bound on a peak stress, which no FLX estimator provides. The first example every author copies teaches a check that cannot pass.
**Evidence:** Contract 6: `peak_stress(p, load, fixed: base.face(role: start_cap))`. FLX: "Point loads, point supports, re-entrant edges and corners ... make exact stresses infinite ... A check on a flagged peak returns `Undecided`"; guaranteed bounds hold "For energy norms" on fitted simplicial meshes, and immersed results are `Estimated`. AGT: "worst margin `peak_stress` 31%"; UIX: "peak_stress < 0.6 × yield: margin 18% ± 4%". Reasoning: where a clamped face meets a free face at a right angle, the linear-elastic stress field is singular, so the peak grows under refinement and FLX's own detector ("a local estimate that fails to decrease under refinement") flags it. Dual-weighted residual estimation needs a differentiable goal, and a maximum is not differentiable.
**Fix:** Rewrite the canonical check over a region that excludes the clamp: `let stress = study.von_mises.max(over: p.body.away_from(base.face(role: start_cap), 2 * thickness))`, then `p.require(stress < 0.6 * p.material.yield_strength(at: 20degC))` with default evidence. FLX defines `peak_stress` as a regularized goal (a p-norm or local average over a stated region, with the regularization error in the budget) and states that a raw maximum is never a goal. ING example 3's sign-off row becomes `Estimated`. AGT and UIX reuse the new check.

**Section:** FLX "Solve plans" (D-FLX-5); ING "`require` and checks" (D-ING-12)
**Problem:** FLX derives adaptivity goals from "the checks that read a result", so adding or editing a check changes the pinned `SolvePlan`, the solve's key and every result read from it. A consumer then alters its producer, which reverses the evaluation graph. It also contradicts D-FLX-5 and D-ING-12.
**Evidence:** FLX: "Goals come from the checks that read a result. When a check depends on `peak_stress(part, load)`, that functional becomes an adaptivity goal automatically." D-FLX-5: "A consumer's accuracy demand never triggers an automatic re-solve of the producer". D-ING-12: checks stay out of the dataflow "so that adding a check never changes a design".
**Fix:** Goals are explicit study inputs written in source (`study(..., goals: [...])`). The language service offers a fix, "add this check's functional to the study's goals", that edits source visibly. Delete FLX's sentence. New ING oracle: adding or removing any `require` leaves the key of every non-check node unchanged.

**Section:** CONTRACT 7.2; KLN "Keys and behavior versions", "Progressive results", Rust API (`OpCx::rng`)
**Problem:** The contract's `OpKey` omits fidelity, which KLN's key includes, and neither says how one exact geometry node serves both `Interactive` and `SignOff`. Item 4 ("or it ran in a class other than `CpuCanonical`") can be read to key a `Certified` result by the GPU that assisted it, which defeats that grade. Random streams are keyed by the full `OpKey`, which contains the class, so CPU and GPU runs draw different samples and differ statistically, not just by rounding.
**Evidence:** Contract 7.2 lists five items, none of them fidelity. KLN: "`fidelity` | `Preview`, `Interactive` or `SignOff`"; "Anvil's `Exact` fidelity serves both `Interactive` and `SignOff`, so exact geometry is one shared node"; `pub fn rng(&self, stream: u64) -> Philox4x32; // keyed by the OpKey`. Principle 4 requires cross-class agreement within declared tolerance.
**Fix:** Contract 7.2 adds "6. the effective fidelity, which each operation version maps from the requested fidelity; an operation that ignores fidelity maps all three to one value". Item 4 becomes "the platform class of the result, which is `CpuCanonical` for `Portable` and `Certified` results". `OpImpl` gains `fn effective_fidelity(Fidelity) -> Fidelity`. KLN keys random streams by the class-independent part of the key.

**Section:** ING "Resource limits", "Manifest"
**Problem:** A feature's fuel limit is clamped by "the organization ceiling", which is policy, not source or lockfile. Two organizations evaluating the same key can get `ING6301 FuelExhausted` in one and a value in the other. That deterministic failure is cached and shared.
**Evidence:** ING: "10⁹ steps; `#[fuel(…)]` raises it up to the manifest maximum and the organization ceiling"; manifest comment "per feature call; within the organization ceiling". Contract 7.2: "Deterministic errors are cached".
**Fix:** The effective limit is a function of source and manifest only, and it enters the node key. An organization ceiling below a requested limit is checked at admission. It refuses the Evaluation with an environmental `FuelCeilingExceeded` (R3-03), never a cached `FuelExhausted`. Apply the same rule to the memory and operation-count limits.

**Section:** ING "The incremental contract with Kiln"; KLN "Memoization, verification and backdating" (D-KLN-5)
**Problem:** A feature node's value includes "accumulators and recorded fuel", and backdating compares whole values. Any edit that changes fuel but not geometry (a new `let`, a refactor, a faster loop) marks the feature changed and re-executes every dependent. That defeats early cutoff for the commonest code edits.
**Evidence:** ING: "Its value is the result or failure, plus accumulators and recorded fuel." KLN: "If the new value equals the old one, keep `changed_at` (backdating)".
**Fix:** A node has separate outputs: the result, one per accumulator kind (checks, notes, tolerance sites, PMI) and metadata (fuel, cost). Each output has its own `changed_at`, and dependents record which outputs they read. Metadata is never compared for backdating. Extend `kiln/minimality` with fuel-only edits, after which no dependent re-executes.

**Section:** ING "Previews, drags and incomplete code", "`require` and checks"; KLN "Progressive results"
**Problem:** A feature that branches on a Flux result fails whenever the observed bound cannot decide, which under today's `Indicator` labelling (R3-07) means every interactive update. When a branch does decide at a lower fidelity, its geometry can differ from what sign-off would build. ING lets a release evaluate "sign-off checks even when geometry ran interactively", so released checks can read geometry that sign-off would not produce.
**Evidence:** ING: "a branch on them may stop with `UndecidedBranch` where the exact build would decide ... a release evaluates sign-off checks even when geometry ran interactively". KLN: "Kiln schedules `Preview` first for every demanded target, then `Interactive`, then `SignOff` when the ceiling allows".
**Fix:** Each node's result records the fidelity of the bounds it observed. An `if`, `match` or `where:` on `Undecided` below the subscription's ceiling yields `ResultStatus::Pending` and waits for the next fidelity's node. That node is already demanded, so D-FLX-5 holds. The construct fails with `ING6401` only at the ceiling. A release demands every node at `SignOff`, not only the checks; replace ING's sentence accordingly.

**Section:** CONTRACT 7.1 (`repo`, clean merge); KLN "Merge" (D-KLN-21)
**Problem:** The clean-merge rule tests only checks that "both parents passed". A check added or edited on one side, which the other side's change breaks, therefore merges cleanly and silently. Defining geometric conflict as overlapping changed regions is so coarse that the commonest pair of concurrent edits conflicts (one side edits a dimension, the other adds a feature). "Distance below the merge clearance (default 0 mm)" can never be true.
**Evidence:** KLN: "Every check that passes on both parents passes on the merge"; "the region as the symmetric difference of base and side Bodies ... two regions conflict when their distance is below the merge clearance (default 0 mm)". ING's default check `name` is "Derived from the predicate's source", so editing a predicate creates a check that exists on one side only. Offline rejoin and unprotected branches rely on this driver alone.
