**Section:** CONTRACT 5 (`ApprovalSubject`); KLN "Revisions and lifecycle states" (D-KLN-26), "Change orders" (D-KLN-28); AGT "Acts and approvals" (D-AGT-20); ELX "Software and firmware as BOM items"
**Problem:** The binding `ApprovalSubject` covers only geometry and PMI, so an approved release does not bind the firmware, material, properties, documents or programs it ships. The release plan's digest deliberately excludes the `ChangeId`, so after approval anyone who can push may rebase onto a Change with the same subject but a different Software item binary or Material, and the approval stays valid. KLN's `ItemDefinition` is richer than the contract's subject but is defined only for Parts and Assemblies, and the contract wins where they differ.
**Evidence:** Contract 5: "`ApprovalSubject` [KLN]: `{ base revisions, ItemDefinition GeometryIds with PMI attached by canonical entity number, check-verdict digest …, effectivity, evidence record ids }`". KLN l.490: "A revision's `ItemDefinition` holds the `GeometryId`s of the Part or Assembly with PMI …, the `Material` version, properties, the BOM by value and documents by semantic content" (no rule for Software, Document, `Program` or `Purchased` Items). AGT l.889: "A release plan's digest covers the `ApprovalSubject`'s `ObjectId`, the tag and the effectivity, never the `ChangeId`". ELX l.798: a Software item "records its item number, version, binary hashes, source repository and Change, toolchain". A firmware or material swap changes no `GeometryId` and no PMI, and changes a check-verdict entry only if some check happens to read it.
**Fix:** Contract 5 replaces the second element: "`ItemDefinition` digests of every affected Item (KLN), for every Item kind". KLN defines `ItemDefinition` per kind in one table: Part and Assembly (name-free identity per R9-12, PMI by canonical entity number, `Material` `ObjectId`, properties, BOM by value); Document (semantic content); Software item (binary hashes, software bill of materials digest, `load` bindings, toolchain digest); `Program` (posted text digest and its simulation evidence ids); `Purchased` (approved-manufacturer list entries). Late-bound fields stay placeholders. AGT's release plan digest keeps excluding the `ChangeId`, and `act.commit` refuses a tag target whose recomputed subject differs from the approved one. New oracle KLN-O-CHG-2: swapping a Software item binary, a Material version or a document after approval voids the approval, while a rename with `#[was]` does not.

**Section:** CONTRACT 5 (`Truth`); ING "`Approx<T>` and the decision rule" (D-ING-7); KLN "Progressive results"
**Problem:** Whether a branch on `Undecided` yields `Pending` or the `Failure` `ING6401` depends on the Evaluation's fidelity ceiling, which is in no key. Failures are cached values, and `Interactive` results are written to the shared cache, so a node computed under an `Interactive` ceiling stores `ING6401` under a key that a later `SignOff`-ceiling Evaluation (or another user) hits, and receives a failure instead of `Pending`. Results then depend on which Evaluation ran first, which breaks principle 4 and KLN-O-EQUIV-1.
**Evidence:** Contract 5: "`if` on an `Undecided` fails loudly … at the Evaluation's fidelity ceiling; below the ceiling the node's `ResultStatus` is `Pending`". ING l.466: "At the ceiling it fails with `ING6401 UndecidedBranch`"; ING l.699: a `Failure` … "Kiln caches it like any value". KLN l.143: `Interactive` results are "Written" to the shared cache. Contract 7.2's six key items contain the effective fidelity but not the ceiling.
**Fix:** Make the node's value independent of the ceiling. A branch on `Undecided` at effective fidelity f always yields the cached value `Undecided { needed, fidelity: f }`, which propagates to dependents as `DependencyUndecided` and which `try` cannot catch. The ceiling affects only reporting: Kiln shows `ResultStatus::Pending` while a higher-fidelity node of the same target is demanded under the ceiling, and the Evaluation report raises `ING6401` when none is. Contract 5 `Truth` and `ResultStatus` adopt this wording; ING-O-35 adds "evaluate under an `Interactive` ceiling, then under a `SignOff` ceiling with a warm memo and shared cache; the second shows `Pending`, then the decided value".

**Section:** CONTRACT 2 (Evidence record); KLN "Physical tests and Evidence records" (D-KLN-35); MFG "Inspection and measurement"
**Problem:** Round 1's R3-17 found that a check's outcome for a fixed Change depended on when it was evaluated. The fix, "an evaluation reads the newest valid evidence record", keeps that dependence: two Evaluations of one Change and lockfile differ when a record arrives between them, two trusted builders can disagree, and incremental and cold builds can differ. "Valid" also reads the clock, since a record from an instrument "past calibration is invalid".
**Evidence:** Contract 2: "An evaluation reads the newest valid evidence record and stores its `ObjectId` in the `CheckOutcome`". KLN l.792: "A record from an instrument past calibration is invalid, and checks over it fail with `CalibrationExpired`". MFG l.563 repeats "Evaluation reads the newest valid record". KLN-O-EQUIV-1 requires incremental to equal from-scratch; contract 7.8 requires two builders to produce the same `ObjectId`.
**Fix:** Evidence selection becomes a function of a recorded input. Each Evaluation reads an evidence index at a transaction-log position, the evidence watermark, which is an input cell recorded in the Evaluation report and CI report. Protected branches advance the watermark by an audited ref transaction when records arrive, so a (Change, watermark) pair fixes every outcome, and two builders evaluate at the same watermark. Validity is judged at the measurement time (the instrument's calibration covered the measurement date), never at evaluation time. Contract 2 rewrites the sentence to "reads the newest record valid at its measurement time, up to the Evaluation's evidence watermark". KLN-O-HW-1 adds: two Evaluations at one watermark agree while a record arrives in between.

**Section:** CONTRACT 5 (`Labels`), 7.6 (context labels, free text); KLN "Labels and export control"; AGT "Context labels and write-down", "Instruction authority and untrusted content", "Risk classification", "Auto-merge" (D-AGT-16, D-AGT-17, D-AGT-24)
**Problem:** `integrity` is part of the label lattice that Kiln joins through every derivation, and catalog content, imported files and all third-party package data are untrusted origins. A real product contains catalog parts and imported STEP, so nearly every derived value carries `data_untrusted`, every agent context that reads one is flagged, every agent Proposal is at least R2, and auto-merge never applies. The contract says a human merge endorses typed values, but no rule says how endorsement changes the integrity label of the inputs Kiln joins, so either the flag saturates or it contradicts endorsement.
**Evidence:** Contract 5: "The join takes the maximum level and the union of each set … Labels are joined through every derivation by Kiln". AGT l.750: "Untrusted origins include imported files, supplier, catalog and web content, all third-party package text". AGT l.653 (D-AGT-16): "any content from a `data_untrusted` context is at least R2"; D-AGT-17: auto-merge only for contexts "free of `instruction_tainted` and `data_untrusted`". Contract 7.6: "A human merge endorses structure and typed values, never free text".
**Fix:** Contract 5 states the integrity rule once: integrity attaches to input cells by provenance, and a human merge of the Change that introduced a typed input (a lockfile pin, an Asset, a source span) clears `data_untrusted` on that input's typed values; free text still needs per-span endorsement. Kiln joins integrity from input cells' current endorsement state, so values derived from a merged catalog pin are trusted data, while unmerged supplier submissions, extraction output and `read.value` handles stay `data_untrusted`. KLN-O-LABEL-1 adds two cases: a merged catalog pin yields trusted derived values; the same pin on an unmerged branch does not.

**Section:** ING "Checks" (`name` field, waivers); KLN "Proposals and merge" (`Conflict::Check { check: CheckId }`), "Diff, large assemblies and references"; CONTRACT 5 (`ApprovalSubject` check-verdict digest), 2 (Evidence record "addressed by the check it serves")
**Problem:** Check identity carries approvals, merge verdicts, metric diffs, evidence addressing and waivers, but nothing defines it. ING's default name comes "from the predicate's source", so the commonest edit, changing a limit from `0.6 * sy` to `0.65 * sy`, creates a new check: the merge rule then sees one check removed and another added rather than a verdict change, and Evidence records addressed to the old check stop applying silently. Two `require`s with equal predicate text collide, and `#[waive(check: "static_margin")]` names a check by bare name across the whole design.
**Evidence:** ING l.844: "`name` | From the predicate's source | Identity across edits; Kiln's diff and merge match checks by it". ING l.847: `x.require(…)` carries the check "into assemblies with the Instance path in its identity". KLN l.395 uses `CheckId`, which no tab defines; contract 5 lists "check id" in the approval subject.
**Fix:** Contract 5 defines `CheckId` = (the attachment's `OpSite` or Instance path, the `require` statement's text-derived identity under contract 5's statement rule, the `name` if written). The default never derives from predicate text, so editing the predicate keeps identity and the merge rule compares verdicts. Two checks with one identity in one attachment fail with a new `ING1103`. `#[waive]` takes the check's binding or full `CheckId`, never a bare name. ING-O-27 adds: editing a check's limit keeps its `CheckId` and its Evidence records.

**Section:** CONTRACT 4 ("frozen by content hash"); KLN "Scope and the operation contract" (D-KLN-2); ANV "Behavior versions" (D-ANV-18); FLX "Kernels, back ends and determinism"
**Problem:** Three mechanisms define what keeps an operation version's bits fixed, and the one Kiln enforces is the weakest. ANV freezes each version's source modules by hash; KLN accepts any code change whose outputs on a conformance corpus are unchanged; FLX only states the policy. A change in a shared result-affecting crate (`linalg`, the `kernels` back ends that compile std forms ahead of time, `simd`) that alters outputs outside the corpus keeps the key and silently poisons every cache that holds the old bits, across tenants.
**Evidence:** Contract 4: "Each operation version is frozen by content hash once released." ANV l.52 (D-ANV-18): "Each operation version, and every internal module it uses (for example `ssi@4`), is frozen by source hash". KLN l.37 (D-KLN-2): "Each operation version registers a digest of its outputs over a conformance corpus, and CI fails when code changes the digest without a version bump." FLX l.344: "Any output-bit change … is a new behavior version", with no freeze mechanism.
**Fix:** Contract 4 adopts ANV's rule for every operation: a released version freezes its source closure, meaning its own modules plus versioned modules of every result-affecting first-party crate it calls (`linalg@n`, `kernels` back end `@n`, `simd` horizontal ops `@n`), recorded as a closure hash in the operation registry. A change to a frozen module creates a new module version used only by new operation versions. KLN's registration refuses a released version whose closure hash changed; the corpus fingerprint remains a second check. Toolchain and `detmath` upgrades keep ANV's golden-hash rule, which correct rounding makes sound for `detmath` only. KLN-O-FPRINT-1 adds: a seeded change in `linalg` outside the corpus is refused by the closure hash.

**Section:** ING "The Ingot IR and Kiln" item 5 (overrides); KLN "Graph model", "Keys"; AGT `evaluate.*` methods; PLT `PoolLane`; UIX D-UIX-15, D-UIX-27; MEC sketch drag; ELX router
**Problem:** The drag path, the most latency-critical path in the product, has no owner in Kiln or `api`. Literal overrides are input cells per ING, but KLN never mentions them, and a feature node's key (module code hashes, argument identities, `OpSite`, limits) does not include an override of a literal inside the feature's own body, so an overridden result can be stored and served under the un-overridden key. UIX, MEC and ELX route per-pointer tools through an "interactive edit lane" and an `api` edit stream that neither PLT's lanes nor AGT's catalog define.
**Evidence:** ING l.753: "A request may carry literal overrides keyed by `LiteralSite` … Kiln treats them as input cells". KLN l.54 lists input cells without overrides, and the word appears nowhere else in KLN. AGT l.312: `evaluate.build` takes "Targets, `Fidelity`, `estimate_only`". UIX l.593: tools "run in the engine process on an interactive edit lane and stream geometry each frame through `api`"; MEC l.180: "`api` Edit stream at 60 Hz"; PLT l.293: `pub enum PoolLane { Foreground, Background }`.
**Fix:** KLN adds overrides to its input cells and to rule 4 of "Keys": a node's key includes the canonical encoding of the overrides whose `LiteralSite` lies in its own code, and results computed under overrides are never written to the shared cache. AGT adds `evaluate.subscribe { targets, overrides, ceiling }` and an `edit.stream` method (a session-scoped stream of override updates ending in one `edit.apply`). PLT adds a third `PoolLane`, `Interactive`, preempting `Foreground` work at node boundaries, which KLN's priority table maps from the drag lane. ING-O-12 and KLN-O-PROG-1 add: a drag's overridden result never answers a request without the override.

**Section:** ECO "First-party WIT packages" (`crucible:host`, `crucible:geom`, `crucible:field`); CONTRACT 4 and 7.4 (evaluation worlds); KLN "Labels and export control"
**Problem:** ECO gives evaluation-world components `crucible:host/cas`, `crucible:geom/measure` and `crucible:field/sample`, which reach the engine outside `crucible:ops`. A component that can read any CAS object by `ObjectId` can read data whose label never joined its node's label, so its outputs can carry content at a lower label than its sources; and measurements and samples taken outside `crucible:ops` are not recorded Op dependencies. ING states there is "no second path to the engine".
**Evidence:** ECO l.358: "`crucible:host` | `diagnostics`, `progress` (write-only), `cas`, `parallel` | | KLN"; ECO l.356: "`crucible:geom` | `types`, `build`, `measure`". ING l.946: "Operation calls go through `crucible:ops/anvil` and `crucible:ops/flux`, served by Kiln as recorded Op dependencies | No second path to the engine". Contract 5: labels "are joined through every derivation by Kiln".
**Fix:** `crucible:host/cas` reads only objects reachable from the call's input handles (capability-style handles, never raw `ObjectId`s), and every read is recorded as a dependency whose label joins the node's. Measurements and samples that compute are `crucible:ops` operations (`anvil::measure_*`, `flux::sample`); `crucible:geom` keeps types and builders only, as D-ECO-7 already says of it. `crucible:host/parallel` is specified by PLT with the determinism rule of its combinators. KLN-O-LABEL-1 adds: a component holding a hard-coded `ObjectId` of a confidential object cannot read it.

**Section:** CONTRACT 7.1 (label invariance), 7.2 (last paragraph); KLN "Keys" rule 2 and `OpCx::rng`; FLX "General operations for non-variational methods"; COV "Platform notes" (Monte Carlo determinism); ELX "Analyses and results"
**Problem:** The keying of random streams is stated four ways, and two of them break other rules. Contract 7.2's "class-independent part of the key" still contains `ObjectId`s, which hash names, so it contradicts 7.1's label invariance; FLX keys streams "by the Op key", which includes the class, so CPU and GPU runs draw different samples (round 1's R3-11). Only KLN's form is consistent.
**Evidence:** Contract 7.2: "Random streams are keyed by the class-independent part of the key." Contract 7.1: "random seeds come from geometry, topology and argument values, never from names." FLX l.450: "counter-based random streams (Philox, keyed by the Op key)". COV l.782 and ELX l.523: "keyed by the class-independent part of the Op key". KLN l.74: "keyed without class, fidelity or names (by `GeometryId`s and argument values)".
**Fix:** Contract 7.2's sentence becomes KLN's: "Random streams are keyed by the operation identity, argument values and input `GeometryId`s or name-free content hashes, never by class, fidelity, `ObjectId`s of named values or `OpSite`s." KLN owns the mechanism (`OpCx::rng`); FLX, COV and ELX replace their sentences with one line pointing to KLN. ANV-O-LABEL-1 adds a Monte Carlo golden check under re-randomized names.

**Section:** KLN "Live documents" (D-KLN-22) against "Labels and export control"; CONTRACT 7.1 (`repo`, live replication)
**Problem:** Live replication splits blocks by label, but KLN's labels attach to repositories, paths, Items, records and CAS objects, not to blocks, and nothing defines what an uncleared principal's local repository, compile or Git export holds for a file whose blocks carry a higher label. The desktop is local-first and authoritative for unpushed work, so an uncleared engineer must hold a `SourceFile` they may not read, or an undefined partial one, and cannot compile the module.
**Evidence:** KLN l.439: "blocks labelled above a document's label live in a separate document that only cleared participants receive". KLN l.673: labels "attach to repositories, paths, Items, records, CAS objects and API responses". KLN l.347: `SourceFile` is "Canonical Ingot text, a block map … and span integrity provenance", one object per file. D-KLN-33: "the local repository is authoritative for unpushed work".
**Fix:** The unit of a source label is a module (one file). A higher-labelled feature lives in its own module; its public signature may carry a lower, declassified label, so uncleared principals compile against the signature and evaluate it through derived views on cleared workers (D-KLN-31's remote evaluation). The live document unit becomes (package, module label set), which keeps contract 7.1's rule. KLN states this in Labels and export control, and KLN-O-LABEL-1 adds: an uncleared clone compiles and evaluates a design whose ITAR module it cannot read.

**Section:** KLN "Changes and refs" (`Change` row); "Electronic signatures" (D-KLN-42)
**Problem:** The `Change` object includes its signature and `ChangeId` is the object's `ObjectId`, so the signature is part of the identity. D-KLN-42 requires dual signing by phase 2 and re-timestamping long-retention records before an algorithm retires. Adding an ML-DSA signature or a new timestamp to an existing Change would change its `ChangeId` and every descendant's parent pointer, rewriting history and voiding every tag, Proposal and signature that names it.
**Evidence:** KLN l.345: "`Change` | Parents, tree, author, … conflicts, signature; `ChangeId` is its `ObjectId`". D-KLN-42: "long-retention records are re-timestamped into an evidence chain before an algorithm retires"; contract 7.8: "Every signature record carries an algorithm id".
**Fix:** Signatures over Changes are detached signature records naming the `ChangeId`, which hashes the unsigned Change; a Change may gain signatures and timestamps without changing identity. The same rule holds for tags, release records, Evidence records and every signed CAS record: identity covers content, and signatures are records about it. KLN-O-SIG-2 adds: adding a second-algorithm signature to a year-old Change leaves every `ChangeId` and tag unchanged.

**Section:** CONTRACT 5 ("Two identities for every named value"); ANV "Two identities and two stages" (D-ANV-24); KLN "Revisions and lifecycle states"
**Problem:** The contract promises a `GeometryId` for every named value, but only Bodies have one. Revision identity, approval subjects and interchangeability use "`GeometryId`s of the Part or Assembly", and an Assembly's identity must drop Instance names and paths, order Instances without names and include placements and mates. Nobody defines that encoding, so renaming an Instance either changes an Assembly's revision definition or relies on an unwritten rule.
**Evidence:** Contract 5: "Two identities for every named value: `GeometryId` hashes the canonical encoding with names, lineage and name-keyed attributes removed". ANV l.136 (D-ANV-24): "Every Body has a `GeometryId` beside its `ObjectId`". KLN l.490: "the `GeometryId`s of the Part or Assembly". MEC owns `Part`, `Assembly` and `Instance` (contract 5).
**Fix:** Contract 5 states the rule for each named type, and MEC owns the encodings: a Part's name-free identity hashes its Body's `GeometryId`, Material `ObjectId`, properties and PMI by canonical entity number, without name or item number; an Assembly's hashes the canonically ordered multiset of (child identity, placement, mates by canonical entity number) without Instance names or paths; Fields keep FLX's (`GeometryId` plus canonical numbers). ANV-O-LABEL-1 extends to Assembly identities under re-randomized Instance names.

**Section:** COV "Materials system", "Data model" (D-COV-13); ING "`Approx<T>` and the decision rule"; CONTRACT 6 (canonical example)
**Problem:** D-COV-13 makes a property read's value depend on the check that consumes it: the read resolves to the lower or upper basis by the sign of that check's sensitivity. Ingot is pure and strict, so `let sy = p.material.yield_strength(at: 20degC)` has one value before any check runs, and one binding feeding two checks of opposite sign cannot hold both. ING has no type or rule for this, and the canonical example's check depends on it. It also violates D-FLX-5 ("a consumer never changes its producer") and makes check evaluation need derivatives through every solve that reads a property.
**Evidence:** COV l.641: "Property reads resolve to a statistical basis on the side the check needs. Form-level derivatives give the sign of the check's sensitivity". ING contains no mention of basis or of sensitivity-resolved values. Contract 6: `p.require(stress < 0.6 * p.material.yield_strength(at: 20degC))`.
**Fix:** A property read returns `Approx<Q>` whose `input and tolerance` part is a `Guaranteed` enclosure from the lower to the upper basis value under the policy's basis (specification limit, else B-basis). The existing decision rule then decides conservatively with no consumer dependence: `x < 0.6 * sy` is `True` only if it holds at the lower basis. Where the property feeds a solve, Flux propagates the enclosure as an input part (by sensitivity sign at the frozen discretization, or by solving at both ends when the sign varies), which is D-COV-13's computation moved into the producer. Check reports name the basis and the side that decided. COV revises D-COV-13; ING adds one row to the decision-rule table; ING-O-8 adds a two-check case.

**Section:** KLN "Revisions and lifecycle states" (release guard); CONTRACT 7.6 ("Passing every check"); ING "Checks" (`severity` row)
**Problem:** Three texts state what blocks a release, and they disagree. KLN requires every check, of any severity, to hold a non-provisional `Pass` or a signed waiver, and says nothing of conditional passes. ING says only `Error` blocks; the contract's agent rule counts a conditional `Pass` only under a covering policy allowance. The policy allowance itself, the record that turns a conditional `Pass` into a gate pass, has no schema, signer or phase in KLN, which owns repository policy; it appears only in KLN's interface row to COV.
**Evidence:** KLN l.507: "Entering `Released` requires every check to hold a non-provisional `Pass` on a release-accepted class or a signed waiver". ING l.841: "`Error` blocks protected merges and releases; `Warning` and `Info` report". Contract 7.6: "every `Error`-severity check has the verdict `Pass` at its declared fidelity, a conditional `Pass` counting only under a covering policy allowance". KLN l.852 (to COV): "policy allowances and `min_evidence_level`"; neither term appears elsewhere in KLN. COV l.811 requires "policy allowances with citations".
**Fix:** Contract 5 defines one predicate, `gate_passes(outcome)`: severity `Error`, non-provisional, verdict `Pass` with every `conditional_on` component covered by a policy allowance, on a release-accepted class, or a Waiver (R9-15). KLN defines `PolicyAllowance { error_source, scope (check kinds, Items, model families), allowance as an `Estimated` component, citation (code and clause), signers }`, a policy-package record changed only through `propose.policy` with two signers, in phase 1 because GP1's checks are conditional on model form. Contract 7.6, KLN's release guard and merge queue, and ING's `severity` row cite the predicate instead of restating it. KLN-O-PLM-1 adds a `Warning`-only failure that must not block, and a conditional `Pass` without an allowance that must.

**Section:** ING "Checks" (`#[waive]`); KLN release guard ("signed waiver"); COV "Policy by zone" (human waiver in the change order); MFG "Sustainability and compliance" ("a person records a time-bounded waiver"); ELX "Electrical rule checks"; KLN, MEC and ELX parts-policy waivers
**Problem:** "Waiver" is one concept with four mechanisms and no glossary entry: a source attribute any editor can write, a signed waiver at release, a human-only waiver in the change order for envelopes, and recorded waivers for parts policy. Which one a release accepts, who may author it, how it expires and what it names differ by tab, and agents can write the source form, which then shows as a waived status in ELX's requirement view.
**Evidence:** ING l.853: "A waiver is an attribute, `#[waive(check: "static_margin", reason: "…", until: "C")]`". KLN l.507: "or a signed waiver". COV l.168: "Human waiver with rationale; agents cannot waive". MFG l.651: "unless a person records a time-bounded waiver in the change order". ELX l.792: status "waived with a reason".
**Fix:** Contract 2 adds **Waiver**: a signature record by an authorized human naming a `CheckId` (R9-05), the Items and effectivity it covers, a reason and an expiry (revision, date or serial range), attached to a Proposal or change order. `#[waive]` in source is only a request that review shows; it counts nowhere until a matching Waiver record exists. Agents may write the attribute, never the record; `Protected` checks and `Refuse` envelopes accept none. ING, KLN, COV, MFG, ELX and MEC cite the entry instead of defining their own.

**Section:** ING Open questions 3 ("Instances at geometry-driven positions"), "Assemblies, variants and families" (D-ING-22); MEC "Standard parts and fasteners" (`fasten`); KLN "Effectivity and variants" (D-KLN-27)
**Problem:** ING's existence rule forbids an Instance whose existence depends on a computed value, which rules out one fastener per hole of a resolved query. MEC's std `fasten(cover_holes, …)` does exactly that, so the two tabs contradict each other on the commonest assembly operation of GP3, GP4 and GP8. ING's proposed answer (a configuration count plus a check against the resolved holes) makes every added hole a two-place edit.
**Evidence:** ING l.1280: "Static Instance existence (D-ING-22) forbids a fastener per hole of a resolved query. Proposal: the count comes from a configuration parameter and a check compares it with the resolved holes". MEC l.513: `let joint = fasten(cover_holes, spec: FastenerSpec::iso4762(…))`, which "picks the shortest standard length" per hole. ING l.589: "Creating an Instance under any other condition, including a loop over a computed count, fails with `ING2601`".
**Fix:** Decide: separate a usage's existence from its multiplicity. An Instance group created by iterating a resolved query is one usage whose existence follows the static rule (configuration parameters and constants) and whose multiplicity and per-member parameters (length, placement) are computed. The 150% BOM keeps its SAT checks over usage existence and lists the group with a computed quantity per configuration point, which BOMs already express as a quantity line. A group may be empty only if its usage declares `min: 0`. ING revises D-ING-22 and `ING2601` to name this exception; MEC's `fasten` returns such a group; KLN-O-PLM-5 adds a bolt-circle fixture whose quantity follows a hole-count parameter.

**Section:** ING "Arithmetic on tolerances" (symbol keys, `.rss`, `.monte_carlo`); CONTRACT 7.1 (label invariance)
**Problem:** Tolerance noise symbols are keyed by site and by the realizing Part or Instance path, and the site is an `OpSite`, so both keys are names. ING does not fix the order in which `.rss` sums symbols or how `.monte_carlo` draws per-symbol streams, so a name-keyed order or stream makes statistical check values depend on names. ANV-O-LABEL-1 requires identical check values after re-randomizing names, which `max_clearance_stat`-style checks would then fail.
**Evidence:** ING l.399 to 401: "A tolerance forwarded into a Part is keyed by (site, realizing Part or Instance path)"; "A tolerance read from geometry … is keyed by the aspect's `EntityId` and Instance path". Contract 7.1: "An operation's geometry, connectivity, Field values and statistics are invariant under any injective renaming … random seeds come from geometry, topology and argument values, never from names." ANV l.935: ANV-O-LABEL-1 checks "identical `GeometryId`s and check values".
**Fix:** Symbol identity stays name-keyed for correlation (which symbols are the same), but every numeric use orders and seeds by name-free keys: a realized symbol by (the realizing Instance's name-free identity and placement, the aspect's canonical entity number, the site's nominal and deviation), an unrealized one by its nominal, deviation and canonical position in the affine form. `.rss` sums in that order through `det_sum`, and `.monte_carlo` draws each symbol's stream from that key. ING-O-7 adds a re-randomized-names case.

**Section:** ING "The Ingot IR and Kiln" item 1; KLN "Graph model" (node-kind table)
**Problem:** The two tabs key the front-end stage differently, and KLN's key is circular. KLN keys it by the module code hash, which is a hash of the IIR the front end produces. ING keys it by "module identity and compiler behavior version", but says compiler releases may change diagnostics, so a shared front-end result can carry another compiler's diagnostics.
**Evidence:** KLN l.58: "Front-end stage | Module code hash, language behavior version | IR and diagnostics". ING l.747: "Each module's code hash is a SHA-256 Merkle hash over its IIR". ING l.749: "Kiln keys each module's front end by module identity and compiler behavior version". ING l.1029: "compiler releases may change diagnostics and speed, never values, failures or fuel".
**Fix:** One rule, stated in ING and pointed to by KLN: a front-end stage is keyed by the source file's content hash, the language behavior version, the compiler release and the interface hashes of imported modules; its outputs are the IIR (identified by the module code hash) and diagnostics as separate outputs. Only the IIR output is shared across compiler releases, which is safe because releases never change IIR semantics; diagnostics are recomputed per release. KLN's table row changes accordingly.

**Section:** ING "Rust features and Wasm components" (the `involute_profile` example, D-ING-15); KLN "Scope and the operation contract" (`OpCx`)
**Problem:** The `#[ingot::feature]` example passes `&mut OpCx` into a Rust function that compiles to a Wasm component and calls `ctx.site`, `ctx.site_keyed` and `ctx.planar_builder`, none of which KLN's `OpCx` declares. `OpCx` is the native operation context in `base`, holding runtime handles; a sandboxed, out-of-process Wasm component cannot hold it. The guest SDK, the one surface third-party authors build against, is therefore unspecified.
**Evidence:** ING l.930 to 934: `ctx: &mut OpCx, // supplied by the host`; `ctx.planar_builder(Plane::XY, ctx.site("profile"))`; `ctx.site_keyed("flank", i)`. KLN l.24 to 30 lists only `checkpoint`, `rng`, `det`, `work_budget` and `fidelity`. PLT l.23: "`OpCx` in `base` wraps PLT's runtime handles (cancellation, budget, pool lane, GPU device)". Contract 7.4: third-party Wasm components run out of process.
**Fix:** ING names a guest type, `ingot_sdk::Cx`, generated by `ingot-bindgen` over the `crucible:ops` and `crucible:host` imports, with `site(name)`, `site_keyed(name, key)`, typed builders for operations and `seed()`; it is the only context a `#[ingot::feature]` function receives. `OpCx` stays native-only. ING states the guest API in one table (method, WIT import, failure), and ING-O-17 checks that the generated SDK matches the WIT.

**Section:** ING "The query language" (custom filter row, D-ING-8) against "`Approx<T>` and the decision rule"; CONTRACT 5 (`Truth`)
**Problem:** ING gives two semantics for `where:` on `Undecided`. The decision-rule section and the contract make it `Pending` below the ceiling and `ING6401` at it; the query section and D-ING-8 make it fail with `ResolveError::Ambiguous` at once. A resolver cannot implement both, and the choice changes whether a query over a Flux result waits or fails at `Interactive`.
**Evidence:** ING l.466: "Below the Evaluation's fidelity ceiling, an `if`, `match` or `where:` on `Undecided` yields `ResultStatus::Pending`". ING l.537: "Custom filter | `where: |f| f.area() > 2 * hole_area` | … `Undecided` fails with `ResolveError::Ambiguous`". D-ING-8: "arbitrary predicates are an explicit `where:` closure whose undecided outcomes fail". Contract 5: "One decision rule, owned by ING and used by `if`, `require` and query `where:`".
**Fix:** Keep the contract's rule. The query row and D-ING-8 say: an `Undecided` filter outcome follows the decision rule (R9-02's ceiling-independent value below the ceiling); at the ceiling `anvil::resolve` returns `ResolveError::Ambiguous { entities, needed }`, with fixes to tighten the filter or raise fidelity. ING-O-35 covers a `where:` filter.

**Section:** CONTRACT 3 (principle 1, "No privileged code"), 7.4 (out-of-process third-party Wasm components); PLT "Isolation of third-party Wasm components" (D-PLT-31)
**Problem:** Only first-party Wasm components run in the engine process; every third-party one runs in a sandboxed worker and pays a message per call, including each `crucible:ops` call it makes back into the engine. A third-party slicer, router or CAM strategy that issues thousands of operation calls per invocation is structurally slower than std's equivalent, which principle 1 forbids ("If a user or agent cannot build a feature, neither can the core team"). The contract states no exception and no parity bound, and std's components are never measured under the third-party configuration.
**Evidence:** Contract 7.4: "Only first-party Wasm components … run in the engine process. Every third-party Wasm component runs out of process on every target". PLT l.514: "Sandbox workers read bulk data through read-only CAS maps, so a call costs one message plus the canonical-ABI copy of its arguments." No tab states a round-trip target for `crucible:ops` calls from a sandbox worker.
**Fix:** Contract 3 adds to principle 1: "Process isolation of third-party code is the one permitted difference, and it is bounded: a `crucible:ops` call from a sandboxed worker costs at most 20 µs plus copy on the reference laptop (target), `crucible:ops` offers a batched call form, and CI runs std's Wasm components in the third-party configuration on every release, within 15% of in-process time (target)." PLT owns the targets and an oracle, PLT-O-WASM-n; ECO's tier rule cites them.

**Section:** MEC "Roles, queries and fixes"; ANV "EntityId" (D-ANV-14); CONTRACT 5 (`EntityId`, `FeatureRole`)
**Problem:** MEC says the roles a feature declares (`wall`, `floor`, `counterbore_wall`) enter the `EntityId`. ANV and the contract hash only the operation's role (`start_cap`, `side(e)`), with feature roles attached as `FeatureRole` aliases. The two rules hash different inputs, so a std feature and Anvil would give one face two ids, and a feature that changes its internal operations (a hole moving from `extrude` to `revolve`) renames its faces under ANV's rule but not MEC's.
**Evidence:** MEC l.47: "`hole` creates `wall`, `floor`, `counterbore_wall` and `countersink`. Roles enter the `EntityId` (contract section 5)". ANV l.319: "the role comes from the operation's vocabulary (`start_cap`, `end_cap`, `side(e)` for `extrude`)". Contract 5: `EntityId` is a "hash of (kind, `OpSite`, role, generating entity ids, discriminator)"; "Features may attach role aliases (`FeatureRole`) to entities they return."
**Fix:** Keep ANV's rule, which the contract states, and fix MEC's sentence: "Feature roles are `FeatureRole` aliases; queries match them, and `EntityId`s hash the operation's role." MEC adds the consequence for stability: a std feature that changes its internal operations needs a major version (ING's semantic-version table already lists changed entity names).

**Section:** CONTRACT 5 (`Truth`, `CheckOutcome`), 2 (Evidence record, Evidence level); ING "Checks" (`evidence` field); COV evidence levels
**Problem:** "Evidence" names three concepts in the core types: the bound kind a check accepts (`evidence: Estimated`), the Evidence records a check read, and a model's Evidence level. `CheckOutcome` has one field called `evidence`, and the contract uses the word both ways, so a builder cannot tell whether the field holds a bound kind or record ids. The glossary separates Evidence level from Evidence record and then the contract and ING reuse the word for a third meaning.
**Evidence:** Contract 5: `CheckOutcome` "`{ verdict, fidelity, evidence, value, limit, margin, severity, source }`"; `Truth`: "disjoint enclosures decide, subject to the check's declared evidence". Contract 2: an evaluation "stores its `ObjectId` in the `CheckOutcome`". ING l.843: "`evidence` | `Estimated` | The weakest bound kind that may decide … never a model's Evidence level (COV)".
**Fix:** Rename the bound-kind concept `decides_on` (values `Estimated`, `Guaranteed`) in the `require` syntax, contract 5 `Truth` and `CheckOutcome`; give `CheckOutcome` a separate `evidence_records: Vec<ObjectId>` field. "Evidence" then means only Evidence records and, in "Evidence level", COV's scale; the contract glossary adds "evidence" for bound kinds to the Never-call-it column.

**Section:** CONTRACT 12 (crate map), 5 (types without a named crate default to `base`); ANV "Crates"; FLX "Domains and values", "Sampling and operations" (`Sampler`)
**Problem:** The crate map's layering cannot hold for the `field` crate. `field` sits in Engine core below Geometry, yet `Field` domains are `Body`, `Instances` and `Ports`, a `Part` is accepted as a `Body` domain, and `Sampler` uses Anvil's certified classification. ANV places `Body` in `anvil-ops`, contradicting the contract's default that shared types live in `base`; MEC's `Part`, `Assembly`, `Instance` and `Transform` have no crate, and no tab places `GeometryId` or `EntityId`.
**Evidence:** Contract 12: "Engine core | `kernels`; `field` (`Field`, domains, representations, `Sampler`); `kiln`". ANV l.20: "`anvil-ops` | The `Body` enum, every operation's `OpImpl`". FLX l.83: "Domains are entity sets (`Body`, `Regions`, `Faces`, …, `Instances`, `Ports`)". Contract 5 lead: "shared types live in `base` unless another crate is named"; `Body` [ANV] names no crate.
**Fix:** Apply the `PlacementPolicy` pattern: `base` holds identities and handles (`GeometryId`, `EntityId`, `BodyHandle`, `InstancePath`, `PortId`), plus a `Classify` trait that Anvil implements and `field`'s `Sampler` calls; `Body` itself stays in `anvil-topo`. MEC's `Part`, `Assembly`, `Instance`, `Transform` and `CoordSys` get a crate, `mech-model`, in the Geometry layer. Contract 12 adds both, and PLT's CI runs a layer check that fails on an upward dependency.

**Section:** CONTRACT 12 (`apps/`); AGT "Scope and invariants", "One catalog, several transports"; MFG Open questions 12; KLN "Deployment"; ECO "SDKs, methods and the CLI"; UIX "Snapshots"
**Problem:** Contract 12 is the build plan, and it omits about ten deliverables that tabs depend on: `apps/mcp` and `apps/crew` (AGT), the machine gateway (MFG), the relay and runner gateway (KLN), the hardware runner (KLN, ELX, AGT), the tool runner (ECO), the model gateway (AGT), and the Python, TypeScript and C-ABI SDKs. Two placements are wrong: AGT says `api` owns transports and also that it has "no transport code", and `inspect.render`, an `api` method, runs `apps/renderer`, making a core crate depend on an app, while the contract's `apps/headless-render` appears in no tab.
**Evidence:** AGT l.1036: "`apps/mcp` and `apps/crew` ship as Linux containers". MFG l.914: "Contract 12's crate map lists no gateway app". KLN l.723: "relay and runner gateway from phase 2". ECO l.322: "In a tool runner". AGT l.7: the `api` crate covers "catalog, transports"; AGT l.39: "`core/api` … no transport code. `apps/mcp` serves it". UIX l.289: "`inspect.render` (AGT's method) runs this renderer headless".
**Fix:** Contract 12 lists `apps/mcp`, `apps/crew`, `apps/machine-gateway` (MFG, packaged by PLT), `apps/relay` and `apps/rig-runner` (KLN), `apps/tool-runner` (ECO, PLT) and `apps/model-gateway` (AGT), and `sdk/python`, `sdk/typescript` and `sdk/c` beside the Rust `crucible-sdk` (ECO). `inspect.render` dispatches to `apps/headless-render`, a service that links `apps/renderer`; `api` depends on neither. AGT's l.7 drops "transports".

**Section:** ECO "First-party WIT packages"; the owners' Interfaces sections
**Problem:** ECO assigns six first-party WIT packages to owners whose tabs never mention them, so the interfaces that every importer and evaluation-world Wasm component compiles against have no specification. Versions also disagree: ECO keeps `crucible:` packages at 0.x until names clear, while its own examples, UIX and ING import `@1.0.0`, `@0.1.0` and `@1`.
**Evidence:** ECO l.356 to 364 assign `crucible:geom` to ANV, `crucible:field` to FLX, `crucible:model` to "MEC, KLN", `crucible:host` to KLN, `crucible:api` to AGT and `crucible:tool` to "ECO, PLT"; grep finds none of these package names in the owners' tabs. ECO l.409 to 411: `import crucible:geom/build@1.0.0; … crucible:model/build@1.0.0; … crucible:host/diagnostics@1.0.0`. ECO l.985: "`crucible:` packages at 0.x". UIX l.763: `crucible:ui@0.1.0`; ING l.971: `crucible:physics/solver@1`.
**Fix:** Each owner adds a "WIT interfaces" subsection listing its packages' interfaces, types, failures and phase, with an oracle that the published WIT matches; ECO's table keeps only the index with links. Examples use `@0.1.0` until the freeze in contract 13.1. `crucible:model` is renamed `crucible:product` (it builds product structure, and "model" means a physics model elsewhere).

**Section:** KLN "Cost and budgets"; MFG "Scope, layering and core types"; ECO "Determinism and limits"; PLT "Worlds, calls and failures"; ING "Limits"; ANV work limits
**Problem:** One failure name means two kinds, and one kind has three names. `BudgetExhausted` is an uncached Abort in KLN and a cached `Failure` in MFG; ANV calls MFG's meaning `WorkLimit`. Wasm limit failures are `OutOfFuel`, `StackLimit` and `MemoryLimit` in ECO, `FuelExhausted` and `StackExhausted` in PLT, and `FuelExhausted`, `DepthExhausted` and `MemoryLimit` in ING; ECO also calls memory growth past the maximum a cached `Failure`, while PLT says `memory.grow` returns −1 and the component decides.
**Evidence:** KLN l.156: "Exhausting it is the Abort `BudgetExhausted`". MFG l.63: "`BudgetExhausted` is a cacheable `Failure`". ANV l.28: "reaching one is the deterministic `Failure` `WorkLimit`". ECO l.433: "`OutOfFuel`, `StackLimit` and `MemoryLimit` are cached `Failure`s". PLT l.523 to 525: `FuelExhausted { used, limit }`, `StackExhausted { limit }`, and growth "Decided by the Wasm component". ING l.723 to 725.
**Fix:** `base` holds one catalog of limit outcomes, owned by KLN, which every tab cites: Failures `WorkLimit { kind, limit }` (argument-set search or work limits), `FuelExhausted`, `StackExhausted`, `MemoryLimit` (semantic limits); Aborts `BudgetExhausted`, `DemandDepthExhausted`, `FuelCeilingExceeded`, `ResourceExhausted`. MFG renames its failure `WorkLimit`; ECO adopts PLT's names and PLT's growth rule.

**Section:** FLX "Verification, validity and agreement"; COV "Validity envelopes as data" (zone evaluation row)
**Problem:** Both tabs specify validity-zone evaluation, with different failures and different oracles, while COV's interface row asks FLX to provide it. A check then fails with `Error(Failure)` or `ValidityError::OutsideEnvelope` depending on which implementation runs.
**Evidence:** FLX l.200: "Flux evaluates COV's regime functions into a `Field<Body, ValidityZone>` and `Flag` or `Refuse` checks"; FLX l.215: "`Refuse` gives `Error(Failure)`" (FLX-O-ERR-9, phase 1). COV l.224: "Zone evaluation | A priori screen, a posteriori zones, intersection | `ValidityError::OutsideEnvelope` with escalations | COV-O-ENV-2 | 1". COV l.808 requires "zone evaluation" from FLX.
**Fix:** COV owns the envelope records and the zone semantics; FLX owns the evaluation operation (`flux::validity_zones`). One failure, `ValidityError::OutsideEnvelope { variable, bound, escalations }`, inside `Error(Failure)` for `Refuse`. COV's capability row becomes "Zone semantics" and points to FLX's operation, and COV-O-ENV-2 and FLX-O-ERR-9 merge into one oracle owned by FLX.

**Section:** KLN "Audit and encryption", "Effectivity and variants", Interfaces; AGT "Audit and personal data"; UIX "Review, agents and collaboration"; ELX "Variants"; PLT and FLX sparse factorization
**Problem:** Four facts have two owners or none. KLN and AGT both define the audit-entry schema, with opposite content rules. KLN and UIX each say the other defines review verdicts and comments. KLN and ELX each specify variant analysis with their own oracle. PLT says it provides `linalg` circuit LU while its own D-PLT-34 gives sparse factorization to FLX.
**Evidence:** KLN l.683: audit entries "never labelled content"; AGT l.825: "This tab owns the schema … with full content only for Act plans, approvals and policy changes". KLN l.853 provides UIX "comments, review verdicts" and l.870 requires "Comment anchors and review verdicts" from UIX; UIX l.483: "Review verdicts are `repo` records". KLN l.546 (KLN-O-PLM-5) and ELX l.140 (ELX-O-VAR-1) both check the 150% BOM against brute force. PLT l.838: "`linalg` for circuit LU"; FLX l.854 lists block-triangular LU.
**Fix:** One owner each. KLN owns the audit log and its envelope; AGT owns the `api`-call payload fields inside it; the content rule is KLN's ("ids and digests, never labelled content"), with Act plans, approvals and policy changes stored as separate labelled records the entry references. KLN defines `ReviewVerdict` and `Comment` records; UIX owns `CommentAnchor` and display. KLN owns variant semantics and KLN-O-PLM-5; ELX's row cites it and keeps only its covering-set policy. FLX owns sparse factorization in `linalg` (D-PLT-34), and PLT's row drops it.

**Section:** UIX "Display data" (cluster DAG); ANV "Measurement, analysis and simulation services" (`anvil::tessellate`); ELX "Hardware-in-the-loop" (linearization); FLX "Multibody dynamics"; MEC "Entities and helpers" (`text`); PLT "Paths, text and accessibility" (D-PLT-7)
**Problem:** Three consumers rely on capabilities their producers never specify. UIX's phase 2 renderer needs a cluster-DAG `DisplayPackage` built "as a deterministic Anvil operation", which ANV does not have. ELX's phase 4 control design needs exact linearization of Flux multibody plants, which FLX's multibody and adjoint tables omit. MEC engraves text from "bundled fonts" while PLT says design text uses registry font packages shaped by Parley, and no operation exposes shaping to Ingot.
**Evidence:** UIX l.211: "Its `clusterlod` method builds the DAG as a deterministic Anvil operation with monotone error bounds"; ANV l.794 has only `anvil::tessellate` → "cluster pages" (phase 1). ELX l.639: "Exact Jacobians of the plant DAE through Flux derivatives" (phase 4); FLX's ELX row (l.903) and adjoint table omit multibody. MEC l.85: "Driven glyph outlines from bundled fonts"; PLT l.70 (D-PLT-7): "fonts from registry packages pinned in `ingot.lock` and shaped by the pure-Rust Parley stack".
**Fix:** ANV adds `anvil::cluster_dag` (phase 2) with monotone error bounds and its oracle. FLX adds `flux::linearize_multibody` (phase 4), `Differentiable`, with a Taylor-test oracle. PLT's D-PLT-7 is the rule; ANV adds `anvil::text_outline(font package, string, layout)` over Parley's shaping, and MEC's `text` calls it with `FontMissing` as its failure.

**Section:** AGT capability tables ("Branch confinement", "Server-side enforcement", "Release Acts", "Data-release family") and Phasing; KLN "Security", "Electronic signatures", "Supplier packages and derived views"; ECO "Recipient watermarking"
**Problem:** AGT phases its safety mechanisms earlier than the KLN and ECO capabilities they run on, so AGT's gate oracles cannot pass when AGT says. Server-side scope, label and approval enforcement is phase 0 in AGT but identity, authorization and labels are phase 1 in KLN; release Acts rest on "KLN signature records" in phase 1 while signature records are phase 2; the data-release family promises watermark and expiry in phase 1 while KLN and ECO deliver them in phase 3.
**Evidence:** AGT l.30: "Server-side enforcement | Scopes, labels, budgets and approvals checked on every call | … | AGT-O-7 | 0"; AGT l.1111 (phase 0): "AGT-O-1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 16 and 20 green". KLN l.703, l.705, l.707: identity, authorization and labels at phase 1. AGT l.913: "Release Acts | Digest over the approval subject; KLN signature records | … | 1"; KLN l.607: "Electronic signatures | Signature records … | 2" while KLN l.576 says "Every Approval of a release … is a signature record". AGT l.914: "Data-release family | … watermark, expiry … | 1"; KLN l.644 and ECO l.123: watermarks at phase 3.
**Fix:** Phase by the owner. AGT moves policy enforcement to phase 1 (phase 0 keeps the `api` types and a single-principal mode) and splits the data-release row: labels, screening, authorization and audit at 1; watermark and expiry at 3 with KLN and ECO. KLN moves a minimal signature record (signer, meaning, signed `ObjectId`, WebAuthn event, algorithm id) to phase 1, since the GP1 release needs it, and keeps Part 11 mode, re-authentication policy and dual signing at 2.

**Section:** MFG "Sustainability and compliance"; COV "Environmental data"; ING "Assemblies, variants and families" (catalog selections); ECO "Mirrors, licences and the parts catalog"; UIX "Performance, privacy and extension" (telemetry row); CONTRACT 13.2 (phase 1 scope)
**Problem:** Several consumers phase a capability before its producer exists, and two tabs ship in phase 1 what contract 13.2 defers. MFG's embodied carbon and RoHS checks (phase 2) read COV's environmental records (phase 5); ING's catalog selections (phase 1) run over `parts::` packages that ECO delivers in phase 2; UIX ships telemetry in phase 1 on a pipeline PLT builds in phase 2, which the contract defers out of phase 1.
**Evidence:** MFG l.655: "Global warming potential per BOM line from COV's per-material `EnvironmentalRecord`s … | 2"; COV l.744: "Environmental records | … | 5". ING l.654: "Catalog selections | Pure over pinned data … | 1"; ECO l.690: "Catalog-part definitions | `parts::` packages … | 2". UIX l.796: "Telemetry | PLT's opt-in pipeline … | 1"; PLT l.669: "Telemetry pipeline | … | 2"; contract 13.2 defers "telemetry" from phase 1.
**Fix:** Apply contract 13.4's rule (first gate that needs it) to these pairs too, and make the spec check enforce it: every capability row that names another tab's capability carries a phase no earlier than that owner's row. Concretely: COV's environmental records move to phase 2 with MFG (generic factors and declared substances only; database connectors stay at 5); ING's catalog selections take phase 2; UIX's telemetry row takes phase 2.

**Section:** CONTRACT 13.3 (scene capacity, orbit and X-ray rows); PLT "Performance engineering" and Phasing; UIX "Two pipelines", "Frame budgets" (D-UIX-24, k-buffer); KLN "Diff, large assemblies and references"; MEC large-assembly representations
**Problem:** PLT says GP1 and GP2 meet every contract 13.3 row at the phase 1 gate, and a missed row blocks beta promotion, but three tabs deliver the capacity those rows need only in phases 2 to 4. Phase 1 has only a forward renderer, which UIX itself rejects as CPU-bound beyond about 10,000 Instances, while the G1 row asks 100,000; the X-ray row assumes a k-buffer that is phase 2.
**Evidence:** Contract 13.3: "G1 100,000 Instances (1,000,000 on the high band)". PLT l.920: "GP1 and GP2 meet every contract section 13.3 row"; PLT l.770: "A missed row blocks beta promotion | … | 1". UIX l.230 rejects per-object draws as "CPU-bound beyond about 10,000 Instances"; UIX l.285: the X-ray row "includes the k-buffer's second pass", k-buffer phase 2. KLN l.414: "100,000 Instances of 10,000 unique Parts (phase 4 target)"; MEC l.539: large-assembly capacity at 2.
**Fix:** Contract 13.3 gives each row the phase from which it blocks promotion: cold and warm start, selection, drag, rebuild, interactive simulation, input latency, memory and installed size from phase 1; orbit at 5M triangles, X-ray and scene capacity from phase 2 for G1 and G2; the 100,000-Instance assembly open from phase 4. PLT's Phasing and PLT-O-PERF-1 cite the column.

**Section:** ING Open questions 5 ("ELX data modules"); ELX Open questions 10 ("Data-module size")
**Problem:** Both tabs leave open a binary sidecar for large `Schematic` and `Layout` data modules. A second storage format would bypass every mechanism built on Ingot text: block-level merge, the live document, span provenance, text-derived `OpSite`s and Git export, so each would need a binary path.
**Evidence:** ING l.1282: "Layouts of 10⁶ items may parse too slowly as Ingot; the fallback is a binary sidecar keyed by statement identity." ELX l.982: "if very large layouts parse too slowly, ING's binary sidecar keeps their semantics and changes only the file format".
**Fix:** Decide: no sidecar. Data modules use `table { … }` literals whose rows are atomic blocks (ING already makes table rows blocks), parsed by a row-specialized lexer that skips the general tree for rows and builds lossless nodes lazily on edit. Target: 10⁶ rows parsed and hashed in under 1 s natively (ING-O-n, measured on an ELX layout fixture in phase 2, before ELX's phase 3 need). If the target fails, split the module by board region, which merge and live documents already handle.

**Section:** CONTRACT 7.2 ("Failures and Aborts"), section 15 ruling on R3-03; KLN Open questions 9 (R3-03 declined)
**Problem:** The decline of R3-03 rests on archived Wasm builds making retired versions available everywhere, but the contract itself exempts GPU `ClassExact` paths, which have no Wasm build. For those, `OpVersionRetired` depends on which engine release runs the Op, not on its inputs, which is the contract's own definition of an environmental end. As a cached `Failure` it can be stored under a key that an engine still holding the version would answer with a value.
**Evidence:** Contract 4: "only versions that cannot compile to Wasm (GPU `ClassExact` paths) fall back to an `OpVersionRetired` failure". Contract 2 (Abort): "An environmental end to a computation … never cached". KLN l.970 keeps the decline.
**Fix:** Keep `OpVersionRetired` as a typed, catchable `Failure` for the user, with its upgrade fix, but never memoize it or write it to the shared cache; contract 7.2 adds it beside Aborts in "never cached". KLN-O-RETIRE-1 adds: a retired GPU path on one engine and a live one on another give no shared-cache cross-talk.

**Section:** ING Open questions 10 (R2-06 declined); ING "Call sites and names"
**Problem:** The decline of R2-06 is partly sound: call identity by name and occurrence survives appended and wrapped stages. It does not survive inserting a same-name call before others in one statement, which renames every later same-name call's entities, and fillet and chamfer chains in one pipeline are the common case. PMI and GD&T keyed by those `EntityId`s then fail with split policy `Fail` or detach.
**Evidence:** ING l.512: "a same-name call renames only later ones of that name". ING l.1288: "inserting a same-name call renames later same-name calls in its statement".
**Fix:** Keep the decline and close the gap in tooling: structural edits that add a feature already insert a new statement (ING l.1100), and a deny-by-default lint `ING-L-RepeatedStage` flags a statement with two or more entity-naming calls of one name, with a machine-applicable fix splitting it into bindings. ING-O-25 adds the prepend case.

**Section:** ING "Records, enums, traits and collections" (`sum`, `min`, `max`)
**Problem:** ING defines its own canonical reduction ("a fixed pairwise tree over indices"), while contract 7.3 requires every reduction in `Portable` code to follow `det_sum`'s 8-lane tree with blocks of 2,048. The interpreter is `Portable` code, so either ING's tree is `det_sum` and should say so, or the same list sums to different bits in Ingot and inside an operation, and the future code generator has two orders to match.
**Evidence:** ING l.349: "`sum`, `min` and `max` use a fixed pairwise tree over indices". Contract 7.3: "every reduction, scan or cross-lane operation in `Portable` code follows the 8-lane f64 or 16-lane f32 tree of `det_sum`". PLT l.263 defines that tree.
**Fix:** ING: "`sum` is PLT's `det_sum` (contract 7.3); `fsum` returns the correctly rounded sum by exact accumulation." ING-O-1 compares Ingot `sum` with `det_sum` bit for bit.

**Section:** CONTRACT 12 (crate map lead)
**Problem:** "Dependencies point down this list" reads as Platform depending on Contracts, since Platform is the first row; the contract elsewhere calls later rows "above" (`base` exists "so that `kiln` never depends on layers above it", and `repo` is a later row).
**Evidence:** Contract 12: "Dependencies point down this list; apps talk to the engine only through `api`." Contract 5: "so that `kiln` never depends on layers above it".
**Fix:** "Each crate depends only on crates in its own or earlier rows; apps talk to the engine only through `api`." Add a `cargo deny`-style layer check to PLT's CI oracle.

**Section:** KLN "Scope and the operation contract" (`OpCx`); PLT "Deterministic parallel combinators"
**Problem:** One concept carries two type names and one mechanism two API shapes. KLN's `OpCx::checkpoint` returns `Result<(), Abort>` while PLT's combinators return `Result<_, Aborted>`; KLN exposes reductions as `cx.det().det_sum(…)` and PLT as free functions `det_sum(cx, …)`.
**Evidence:** KLN l.25: `pub fn checkpoint(&mut self) -> Result<(), Abort>`; l.27: `pub fn det(&self) -> &runtime::Det; // det_sum, det_reduce, exact_sum`. PLT l.298: `pub fn det_sum(cx: &OpCx, xs: &[f64]) -> Result<f64, Aborted>`.
**Fix:** The type is `Abort` (contract 2's term) everywhere; `ResultStatus::Aborted` stays as the status name. PLT's free functions are the API, and KLN's `OpCx` drops `det()` and points to PLT.

**Section:** KLN "Determinism policy" (D-KLN-11, D-KLN-12, D-KLN-13)
**Problem:** KLN says this section owns only the policy, then restates three of PLT's mechanism decisions with their own rationale: `detmath`, GPU class rules and reduction trees. Two tabs now argue the same facts, which contract 10 ("Say it once") forbids and R3-37 targeted.
**Evidence:** KLN l.221: "Contract 7.3 sets the rules and PLT owns the mechanism table; this section owns the policy". D-KLN-11 (detmath), D-KLN-12 (WGSL and `ClassExact`), D-KLN-13 (`det_sum` and binned summation) restate PLT's D-PLT-15 and contract 7.3.
**Fix:** Decision numbers are stable, so keep D-KLN-11 to D-KLN-13 as one line each: "Superseded by contract 7.3 and D-PLT-n; KLN's policy is the grade and acceptance tables above (revised in round 3)." This frees about 250 words.

**Section:** CONTRACT 2 (Operation, Op), 5 (`OpSite`, `OpKey`, `OpCx`)
**Problem:** The prefix `Op` means three things: an operation (`OpImpl`, `OpCx`, `OpVersionRetired`), an Op node (`OpKey`), and a call site of any feature or `fn` frame (`OpSite`). The glossary separates "operation" from "Op" by one letter's case and then forbids "op" in prose, so readers and agents must infer the meaning from capitalization.
**Evidence:** Contract 2: Operation, Never call it "'op' in prose"; Op: "A node that calls one operation or one Wasm component". Contract 5: `OpSite` "the path of these frames (statement, call, iteration keys) from the Evaluation's root, `fn` calls included".
**Fix:** Rename `OpSite` to `CallSite`, since it identifies every call frame; keep `OpKey` (an Op node's key) and the operation types. The glossary row for Op adds: "Rust types with the `Op` prefix name operations, except `OpKey`." A one-pass rename now costs less than after the crates exist.

**Section:** CONTRACT 7.4 (determinizer)
**Problem:** The contract's list of what the determinizer injects omits growth guards, which PLT adds and which are needed: the Wasm specification leaves `memory.grow` non-deterministic even in its deterministic profile, so a host-caused growth failure seen by a component would otherwise become a cached `Trap`.
**Evidence:** Contract 7.4 lists "fuel metering …, stack-depth limits and NaN canonicalization". PLT l.488: "Guarded `memory.grow` and `table.grow`: host-caused failure below the declared maximum traps with a host-failure marker". The Wasm 3.0 profiles appendix (opened) says `memory.grow` and `table.grow` "technically remain non-deterministic, in order to be able to indicate resource exhaustion".
**Fix:** Contract 7.4 adds "and growth guards that turn a host-caused `memory.grow` or `table.grow` failure below the declared maximum into an Abort".

**Section:** KLN "Proposals and merge" (recursive merge bases); "Audit and encryption" (FIPS 140-2)
**Problem:** Two statements are outdated. Git's `recursive` strategy is now an alias of `ort`, and the FIPS 140-2 move to the historical list is in the past as of this spec's date.
**Evidence:** git-scm.com merge strategies (opened): `recursive` "is now a synonym for `ort` … redirected to mean `ort` in v2.50.0"; `ort` "creates a merged tree of the common ancestors and uses that as the reference tree". NIST's FIPS 140-3 transition page (opened): "All FIPS 140-2 certificates are placed on the Historical List" on 22 September 2026. KLN l.381 and l.689.
**Fix:** KLN l.381: "as Git's `ort` strategy does", citing the merge-strategies page and dropping the [unverified] mark. KLN l.689: "NIST moved FIPS 140-2 certificates to the historical list on 22 September 2026", so FIPS mode accepts only FIPS 140-3 modules.

**Section:** Every tab (contract 11 style rules)
**Problem:** The tabs carry about 1,080 sentences over 25 words and about 340 paragraphs over three sentences, by the spec check's own count, mostly inside decisions; KLN's lead sentence alone runs 33 words. Contract 11 asks for sentences under 25 words and paragraphs of at most three sentences, and the founder's taste requirement makes this more than polish for a spec read by agents.
**Evidence:** `python3 docs/tools/check.py` per tab: ANV 167, KLN 128, PLT 122, AGT 99, UIX 96, ELX 94, ECO 85, MEC 83, FLX 79, ING 72, MFG 41, COV 12 long sentences; FLX 41 and KLN 34 long paragraphs.
**Fix:** Round 3's revision brief sets a hard budget the check enforces as an error: no sentence over 40 words, at most 5% of sentences over 25, no paragraph over four sentences; decisions split *Why* and *Rejected* into short sentences. Leads are rewritten first.

**Section:** Capability tables and Phasing sections named below
**Problem:** Owners and consumers state different phases for the same capability, and two tabs contradict their own Phasing sections.
**Evidence:** Tablets: UIX l.691 and Phasing phase 2, PLT l.147 and ECO l.473 phase 3. Lattice Boltzmann and particles: COV l.309 phase 5 (Wasm) and l.375 phase 6, FLX l.470 phase 4 and l.471 phase 5 (native). ERP and MES connectors: ECO l.563 phase 2, MFG l.632 phase 4. Air-gapped installs: PLT l.601 phase 2, KLN l.758 phase 3. Rust SDK: AGT l.265 phase 1, AGT Phasing l.1111 and ECO l.558 phase 0. FLX flexible multibody: l.646 phase 3, FLX Phasing l.1017 phase 4. FLX sizing Fields: l.139 phase 1, l.503 phase 2. Browser updates: PLT l.561 puts "a transparency log" in phase 1, which contract 13.2 defers.
**Fix:** The owner's row wins and consumers cite it: tablets 3 (PLT owns the targets); lattice Boltzmann 4 and particles 5, native (FLX); ERP and MES connector worlds 2 (ECO), with MFG's mapping at 4 stating it builds on them; air-gapped 3 (KLN's bundles); Rust SDK 0 (AGT corrects its row); flexible multibody 3 and sizing Fields 2 in FLX's own tables; PLT's update manifest uses TUF alone in phase 1 and adds the transparency log in phase 2. The spec check gains a cross-tab phase comparison for capability names shared between tabs.

**Section:** CONTRACT 2 (External input, Catalog part, Evaluation, Change), 7.8; AGT method tables; KLN "Supplier packages"; ECO registry actions
**Problem:** Several names break contract 2's "one name per concept" or its Never-call-it column. AGT's Act types are `ActionPlan` and `ActionReceipt`, though "action" is forbidden for Acts; "data package" means an External input (which the contract's own row both uses and forbids), a registry Package and an outbound supplier shipment; "revision" names source states in the contract and three tabs, though it is reserved for Item revisions; and one Evaluation report has three names in AGT (`EvaluationReport`, `BuildReport`, `CiReport`).
**Evidence:** AGT l.335: "`act.prepare` … → `ActionPlan` with digest"; l.336: "then `ActionReceipt`"; ECO l.653 heads its registry Act table "Action". Contract 2 External input: "a catalog or regulation data package", with "data package" in Never call it; KLN l.625: suppliers "receive signed data packages". Contract 2 Evaluation: "compute a set of nodes for a revision"; contract 7.8: "Trusted builders evaluate only merged revisions of protected branches". AGT l.171 `Final(EvaluationReport)`, l.312 `BuildReport`, l.317 `CiReport`.
**Fix:** `ActPlan` and `ActReceipt`; ECO's column becomes "Act or method". External input examples say "a catalog or regulation dataset"; supplier shipments are "supplier packages" (KLN's own heading); "data package" leaves the spec. Contract 2 and 7.8, PLT l.138 and KLN l.625 say "Change" or "merged Changes". AGT keeps `EvaluationReport` for every Evaluation, with `CiReport` as the Proposal CI record that contains them, and drops `BuildReport`. The spec check's forbidden-term list gains "ActionPlan", "data package" and "revision" outside PLM context.

**Section:** AGT error codes and method catalog; KLN "`api` methods and events"; ECO "Events and webhooks"
**Problem:** Methods, errors and events share the `<group>.<name>` shape, so `propose.policy` (a method) sits beside `propose.policy_unsatisfied` (an error), `read.unknown_handle` reads like a Read method, and error families such as `auth`, `label`, `budget` and `build` look like groups outside the eight. Event ownership has a gap: ECO says KLN defines evaluation event types and AGT the Act types, but AGT defines none and KLN's list has neither.
**Evidence:** AGT l.328: `propose.merge` fails with `propose.policy_unsatisfied`; l.330: the method `propose.policy`; l.307: `edit.revert` fails with `edit.revert_conflict`. Contract 7.6: "There is no other group." ECO l.518: "KLN defines repository, lifecycle and evaluation types, AGT the Act types". KLN l.779 lists no `evaluation.*` or `act.*` event.
**Fix:** Error codes take a distinct form, `<family>/<code>` (`propose/policy_unsatisfied`, `auth/human_only`), documented as a separate namespace from methods. KLN adds `evaluation.completed` and `evaluation.aborted`; AGT adds `act.prepared`, `act.approved`, `act.denied` and `act.committed`, each carrying ids and states only (D-KLN-34).

**Section:** ING Open questions 1 ("Kind granularity") and 2 ("Frequency into phase")
**Problem:** Both questions are open, and the second hides a classic error: `sin(f * t)` with `f` in hertz compiles without the 2π.
**Evidence:** ING l.1278 and l.1279: "Trigonometric functions accept a dimensionless phase, so `sin(f * t)` with `f` in hertz compiles without the 2π. A lint on a `Frequency` factor reaching a phase is proposed."
**Fix:** Question 1: close it with a process, not a list: a new std kind needs an RFC with at least one seeded error it prevents, added to ING-O-4's corpus; the starting set stays as written. Question 2: adopt a deny-by-default lint, `ING-L-HertzPhase`, raised when a product with a `Frequency`-kinded factor reaches a trigonometric argument without passing through `AngularFrequency`; its machine-applicable fix rewrites `f * t` as `f.angular() * t`, where `f.angular()` is 2πf. Add the case to ING-O-4.

**Section:** ING Open questions 4 ("Affine arithmetic at scale") and 6 ("`Decimal` resolution")
**Problem:** Both questions block std numerics that phase 2 freezes.
**Evidence:** ING l.1281: "Stacks over 10⁵ sites may need symbol condensation". ING l.1283: "Is 10⁻⁹ enough for every currency and pricing rule MFG needs?"
**Fix:** Question 4: when an affine form exceeds 4,096 symbols, symbols whose coefficient is below 10⁻⁶ of the form's radius fold into the remainder, which keeps `.limits()` a guaranteed enclosure and loses only their correlation; `tolerances(x)` reports how many folded, and ING-O-7 adds a 10⁵-site stack measured against the exact result. Question 6: keep 10⁻⁹, since currency minor units and per-unit prices of small parts need far fewer decimals [unverified: ISO 4217 table not opened]; specify round-half-even for every `Decimal` product and quotient, and require an explicit `round_minor(currency)` where a value becomes an amount payable, with a lint on unrounded payable amounts.

**Section:** ING Open questions 7 ("Feature granularity"), 8 ("Jacobian types") and 9 ("Literal sites under live edits")
**Problem:** Three design questions remain open before std freezes in phase 1.
**Evidence:** ING l.1284 to 1286.
**Fix:** Question 7: one rule, checked by a std lint: a std helper is a `feature` if it calls an entity-naming operation or returns a value carrying `EntityId`s, a `#[memo] fn` if it is pure and estimated above 10⁶ steps, and a `fn` otherwise. Question 8: `Mat<R, C>` diagnostics name the offending entry `(i, j)` with its expected and actual dimensions and print the row and column dimension vectors once, as an `ING3001` note. Question 9: overrides key by `LiteralSite`, which follows `#[was]`; a concurrent rename writes `#[was(old)]`, so the override maps to the new site and the drag continues. Only a deleted literal ends the drag, with the notice ING describes.

**Section:** KLN Open questions 1 ("Hashing large values")
**Problem:** BLAKE3 for derived values would create a second identity space: one value could have two `ObjectId`s, deduplication and two-builder agreement would compare ids across algorithms, and the reserved algorithm byte exists for migration, not for mixing.
**Evidence:** KLN l.961: "If browsers miss 1 s per GiB, should derived values, which need no FIPS approval, use BLAKE3's tree mode?" D-KLN-14: "with a one-byte algorithm code reserved for migration".
**Fix:** Decide no. Keep SHA-256 for every object; meet the browser target with chunk-parallel `crypto.subtle.digest` across the engine's workers, which KLN already specifies, and if the measured target fails, relax the browser row to the measured value rather than split identities. Remove the question.

**Section:** KLN Open questions 2 ("Sibling order") and 3 ("Designed contact")
**Problem:** Both questions touch merge correctness and are open.
**Evidence:** KLN l.962: "Loro's fractional indices can interleave concurrent sibling inserts; does that misorder features often enough to matter?" KLN l.963: "a 0 mm merge clearance flags them; per-mate exemptions may be needed."
**Fix:** Question 2: statement order in Ingot matters only for definition before use and for the ordinal of unnamed statements in their `OpSite`. After any CRDT merge the reconcile step checks both, and a change to either becomes `Conflict::Text` on the affected block; otherwise order is cosmetic and the formatter keeps the merged order. Question 3: merge conditions 4 and 5 count only positive-volume overlap, and they exempt pairs related by a declared mate or joint (MEC's welds, `fastened`, press fits with a declared interference), so designed contact never conflicts. KLN-O-MERGE-1 adds both cases.

**Section:** KLN Open questions 4 ("Revision rules"), 5 ("Item numbers in source") and 8 ("Definition tolerance")
**Problem:** The default definition tolerance is absolute (0.1 µm), which conflicts with contract 7.1's per-Body scale-relative resolution: Anvil's own table gives a 300 m ship hull a resolution of about 0.48 µm, so for GP13 the default lies below what the Body can distinguish, and every engine upgrade would mark the hull modified. The other two questions are open.
**Evidence:** KLN l.968: "MEC should confirm the default of the smaller of 0.1 µm and 1% of the tightest tolerance." Contract 7.1: "Per-Body scale-relative resolution plus per-entity tolerances; no global tolerance." ANV l.186: "Ship hull | 300 m | 2⁻²¹ m ≈ 0.48 µm | ≈ 0.49 mm" (resolution and growth cap). KLN l.964 and l.965.
**Fix:** Question 8: the default is the smaller of 1% of the Item's tightest tolerance and Anvil's growth cap 2¹⁰ρ (about 0.12 µm for GP1), and never below ρ itself. Question 5: keep item numbers in source through `part(…, item:)`, since BOM nodes read them and records keyed by lineage would need a second identity; under an `External` system of record (D-KLN-39) the connector assigns numbers through a Proposal that edits source. Question 4: the revision-label scheme is policy data in the numbering policy package, with the letters-skipping default marked [unverified] until checked against ASME Y14.35-2025; no code depends on it.

**Section:** KLN Open questions 6 ("Part 11 and AS9100 assessment") and 7 ("End-to-end mode and caching")
**Problem:** Both questions are open; the second decides whether end-to-end customers lose the shared cache entirely.
**Evidence:** KLN l.966 and l.967: "Should a customer-hosted cache tier inside the boundary restore sharing?"
**Fix:** Question 7: yes. A customer-hosted tier 2 store and trusted builders inside the boundary form their own trust domain under contract 7.8, sharing within the customer's tenant only; Crucible's cloud holds no keys. Question 6: the package is contract 7.7's Computer Software Assurance package plus a traceability table from each 21 CFR 11.10 and AS9100 clause to KLN oracles and their results per release; the assessor is the customer's choice, and phase 3's third-party assessment uses one assessor named in the program plan.
